I would've never guessed my wood could produce a bloodcurdling sound like that...
Yeah. The wind played a prank on you.
Thanks a lot, Commander! Now I've got nothing to be scared of!
Need to make up for how behind schedule I am!
Back to work, back to work! Quickly, quickly!
Gotta focus, gotta focus! Here we go, here we go!
You sure get... awfully fired up when you work.
Huh? I'm just working myself up to boost my productivity.
Logging is a really uplifting job. Want to give it a shot, Commander?
Sure. I'm free right now, so I'll lend a hand.
Whew... That's all the wood I needed to chop.
I should give this to O'Brien.
O'Brien, I've got all the wood you asked for.
Great! I'm... really surprised I got to do some logging with you.
I'm just thinking... maybe I should've been more professional. I mean, I must've been pretty loud back there.
Doing it your way is just fine.
Your job feels more rewarding when you're excited about it. Boosts productivity, too. You're doing great.
Out of nowhere, a dull yet very audible sound rings out in the distance.
That noise...
Huh?! What was that? Did you hear it?
It sounded far off... It was like, "Bang! Pow!"
Did something... break? Or maybe fall really hard?
Sounds like it came from over by Rockheap Mine.
Oh no! I worry something might've happened in the mine! Could you go and have a look? I'll be there as soon as I'm done with this wood!
Alright. I'll go look.
John, you alright?
C-Commander! You're here! Ugh...
Man, that freaked me out!
It was the minecart track. I think the spikes holding it together have come loose!
My minecart was chock-full of ore, and when it got here... Bam! Fell from a high height, and the track broke.
Did you get hurt?
Nah, I'm fine! Just spooked me a little, that's all.
I dunno what to do with the track broken, though. I've still got several carts' worth of ore left to haul today, but I won't get anything done with a broken track... I'm screwed!
*sigh*... I don't want it to be my fault that your development plan grinds to a halt...
Don't worry about that. Let's start by looking for a replacement.
Good idea! It's just this section that's broken. If we reconnect 'em, we can get the minecart moving again!
Oh! I just remembered! We can use wood.
You can make tracks using wood?
Yeah. It works. I've done it before.
Got it. I'll go look for some wood you can use.
Hey, O'Brien.
Commander? What brings you back here? What caused the noise? Something in the mine?
John said a part of the track broke, and the minecart fell over. Do you have any wood we can use as a substitute?
Of course. There are very sturdy trees deeper in the forest. The temporary track we had before was even made of wood from them.
Oh, do you have some lying around? Let me see.
Um, Commander... You aren't thinking of using wood that was just chopped to make a temporary track, are you?
Is that a bad idea?
Ahem... It's not going to work. At all.
You need to plan ahead for these things, because you have to dry the wood after it's been cut.
Additionally, you have to reduce the moisture content to raise its stiffness and make it less likely to bend and crack!
Naturally, it's also necessary to weed out the low-quality material...
Only then can you provide the ever-important wood when it's most needed.
Wow... I'm glad to have an expert like you, O'Brien.
Stop, you're making me blush! Anyway, please prepare some premium-quality wood for the stockpile. In return, I'll take some already-processed wood and make a track.
Understood.
O'Brien, here's the wood you wanted.
Great! It all looks excellent! Here's the wooden makeshift track that John needs.
Look at its surface. It's perfectly smooth, and it's in the exact measurements of the track.
Feels pretty dang firm, too.
Mhm. Now, I bet John must be getting impatient.
Please go and deliver this track to her right away!
John, have a look at this.
Whoa... Commander! Is this a makeshift track? It's perfect!
I should be able to meet the quota for today now! But... Aw, man, it's so late...
I won't be able to leave work singing my way home before the day's over, will I, Commander?!
I mean... What can I do?
You wanna hear my clocking-out song, don'tcha?!
Reckon you could help me with a part of my quota for today?
All you've gotta do is prepare the last minecart for me!
Ugh... Okay.
Whew... John, have a look.
Whoa! Perfect, Commander! I just... I dunno how to thank you!
Let me sing you my clocking-out song!
Thanks, but you don't need to.
I do! I've gotta express my gratitude!
Sun's a-come down, hey-hey! After work comes dinner, yay! My giddy gait's like a song, oh yeah♪
My giddy gait's like a song, oh yeah♪
Hmm... Feels a little sad to sing it all by myself.
I can't sing, if that's what you're asking.
That's fine! I've got a friend for that!
Ahem... As thanks for helping me out, what do you say I treat you to dinner tonight?
Windswept Plains cooking?
Yup! Heheh! I'll get a fire going, so could you go and look for my friend in the meantime?
Sure, I guess. Where is this friend?
Head to the river and you should hear the clocking-out song on the wind. She'll be singing it!
Sun's a-come down, hey-hey! After work comes dinner, yay! My giddy gait's like a song, oh yeah♪
...O'Brien?
Commander? Fancy meeting you here. What brings you to the river?
John asked me to come.
Oh. Does she want to challenge me to a fishing competition?
Not so much fishing, but rather eating. She's serving her specialty Windswept Plains dishes.
She's cooking? Alright, then let's go. Delicious food waits for no one!
Heheh... I can already smell it on the wind...
Ah, I nearly forgot – here, have this!
O'Brien suddenly pulls out a piece of paper and shoves it into my hand.
What is it?
Who knows? It's just something that the breeze brought to me while I was working.
And now, it's yours! Maybe it's a treasure map of some sort!
Treasure. Yeah, right...
I'll hold on to it for now, anyway.
Patrick, got any decorative paintings in your collection?
Oh, Commander! Why the sudden interest? I didn't take you for an art aficionado.
Did word get out that I make sketches or something?
No, I'm just asking because I want to add some artistic flair to the harbor.
Anyway, did you just say you make sketches?
Not really! I just doodle in my spare time. I wouldn't go so far as to call them sketches!
But you do draw them yourself? That's even better.
I wanna see you draw. Think you could make a picture for me?
Um... Okay, since you seem pretty keen on this, I could make something just for you.
What do you want me to draw?
Hmm. Tough question. Maybe a landscape or a portrait.
Heh. Sounds like you could use some inspiration.
You should take a stroll around the harbor. The view's great and there's loads to see.
You might come across a scene that makes you think, "I want this on my wall." Want me to accompany you?
Sure. Lead the way.
Commander! Any thoughts on this place?
It's got a great view. Blue sea, blue sky, ships coming and going... You can even see silhouettes of islands in the distance.
It's the perfect place to sketch. Lots of compositions to choose from.
That's exactly what I was thinking.
Since the lighting and angles here are ideal, how about I make it a landscape painting for you?
Hmm... I dunno. Feels like something's missing.
Something to give the picture a soul, I guess. It's like there's no clear focal point.
What? Didn't you want me to make a landscape sketch of the harbor?
Or... do you have a particular scene in mind that you want to see?
No, I don't know exactly what I want. I just think a landscape with nothing else feels lacking.
Ah. I see.
When it comes to creative work, inspiration is a crucial catalyst. You can't force it.
How about we walk some more over there? Who knows – the spark might suddenly come to you in a different place.
I guess we could.
Stephen, you busy?
Commander? Is... Is there a problem with the orders?
No, it's not about orders. Don't be nervous.
See, it's about...
What? A sketch? We're talking about art?
I'm not very well-versed when it comes to art and stuff. All I know is work, cargo, and freighters.
Relax. I'm not looking for expert advice or anything like that.
I'm just looking to get a painting made, but I don't know of what yet, so I'm looking around to see if I can find a place or thing that moves me.
Ah, you're looking for inspiration. Why don't you ask Bremen? She knows loads of things and has unique takes on everything. I think she can help you.
Bremen, you say? I might go to Café Manjuu, then.
Bremen, got a moment?
Welcome, Commander. Here to order something? We got some pretty nice coffee beans not long ago!
Thanks, but no. I was hoping you could give me some advice. Artistic advice.
Um, artistic advice? I'm... not sure if I'll be able to help you with that.
Don't be alarmed. It's not about artistic theory or anything complicated.
It's just about a painting. I want Patrick to make a sketch for me, but I don't have a subject in mind.
So, I came to you, hoping you might have an idea.
Ah, I see. Then let me ask you this: Would you prefer a painting of the bustling vibe of the harbor, with people coming and going...
Or a painting of the tranquility and vastness of the blue sea and sky?
Frankly speaking, I like them both.
A bustling scene is full of life, while a tranquil one has a beauty to it. I can't pick just one or the other.
Okay, well, if you can't pick, why not combine 'em?
Combine them?
Like, how about a scene of cargo being moved at the harbor?
Think about it. The vast and blue sea and sky in the background, anchored ships and people moving around in the middle ground, and cargo being loaded and unloaded in the foreground.
It's got both the magnificence of the sky and the sea, and activity going on. It's the best of both worlds. How's that sound?
A combination of life and tranquility, with people and the landscape melding together... That's a good idea.
Glad I could help.
Patrick, I'm back.
Wow, you sure look happy. You must've found some fantastic inspiration, huh?
Sure did. I asked Bremen for advice, and she helped me figure out exactly what I want.
What do you think about drawing the cargo pier? There's the blue sky and sea in the background, then as the main stars, there're some freighters and Stephen loading and unloading cargo.
Not a bad subject. It's got a balance of life and stillness, and it's the harbor at its essence.
But... I have some bad news.
Bad news? What is it?
It's that... I can't find the brush I always use.
If I'm going to sketch, I'll first need to get a brush that's comfortable to use. What a bummer...
A brush, eh? Not a problem. This island has more or less everything in terms of resources, so making a brush will be easy.
It's done. Give it a try.
You've done it again, Commander! Let me see how it feels...
Hm... Feels comfortable in my hand, and the hairs on the brush tip are soft and bendy. It's even better than my original brush!
I'll start sketching right away! You can find a place to sit and wait or go out for a walk if you want.
I guarantee you'll be happy with the picture once it's done!
Wait a sec... Something just finally dawned on me.
What? What is it? Do we not have enough paint?
No, it's not the paint... It's that we don't have a frame.
We can't just leave the finished painting sitting on an easel forever, can we?
Huh? You could just roll it up, put it in a tube, and bring it with you.
Putting it in a frame just means extra work.
That won't do. I refuse to just roll up something you painted for me.
It needs to be framed and hung up somewhere properly.
Tell you what, you go ahead and start painting. I'll get a frame one way or another.
Heh. You really care about the fine details, Commander.
O'Brien, got a moment?
Commander? What's that you're carrying? Elegant wood?
Yup. I want to get a stunning picture frame for the painting Patrick is drawing for me.
Figured this elegant wood is just the thing for it.
W-wait, are you serious? It's the highest-quality wood on the island. The grain is super fine, it's stronger than steel, and it has such a clear fragrance.
And you're going to make a picture frame with it?
That's right. Its aroma and grain are perfectly suited for it.
Err... I can't deny it when you put it like that. It just feels like a bit of a waste, you know?
I know where you're coming from.
Still, Patrick's painting is something special. It'll depict a precious moment on this island captured in time.
That's why the frame needs to be the best. So we can feel proud about displaying it for all to see.
So, please, take this wood and make a beautiful frame with it. I believe in your skill to make the absolute most of it.
*sigh*... Okay! Just because you insist on it and Patrick's pouring her soul into her work.
Please give me some time. I'll put everything I've got into it!

sequence: Sometime later...

scripts.say: It's done! Have a look, Commander. It fits like a glove, and the corners are rounded so they won't hurt your hands.
I even polished the surface to the point where you can see your reflection in it! And I did it without affecting the wood's fragrance!
It's perfect – better than I could've imagined, even. Thank you.
I'm glad to hear you like it. Bring it to Patrick so she can see it, too.
Will do. See you later.
Knock yourself out. See you, Commander!
Patrick, are you done painting?
Yup, I'm done! Here it is – I call it, "The Porter at the Harbor."
Whoa. It's incredible. The light, the shadows, the movement, the atmosphere... They're all so true to life.
Right? It wasn't easy capturing a moment of Stephen hard at work.
Yeah. You really outdid yourself. Here, have a look at the frame. What do you think of O'Brien's handiwork?
It's really beautiful. So much more ornate than any off-the-shelf frame I've ever seen.
Shall we put the painting in?
Yeah, let's!
There we go. No beautiful painting is perfect without a beautiful frame to go with it.
Heheh. Do you really like my art that much?
Of course I do. It's gorgeously made and carries a lot of meaning.
Then I'll tell you what – after putting so much work into it, and after you went through the trouble to provide a frame for this painting... I'll let you have it for free!
Buuut... don't you have something to say?
Anything you'd like? Coffee? Or maybe snacks?
Oh boy! I'll just tidy up here, then what do you say we relax at Café Manjuu?
When you've finished a big job, you should kick back and relax for a while.
Ah, right, I nearly forgot! Here, take this, Commander.
What is this? Feels like... cold, hard, treated leather. Or is it some kind of special paper?
Just something I found while sorting through newly-arrived cargo at the harbor.
It was stuck between some boxes. What do you do with it? Beats me!
All I know is that, when I picked it up, I got a hunch that you'd find a way to put it to use.
An artist's gut feeling, huh? It's covered in dark brown lines, but they're warped. It could be a map or some encoded message, but I can't make sense of it.
Yeah, I'm stumped... But if you want me to hold on to it, then I will.
Huh? Did it freeze?
There is a bang from the nearby servers, followed by a sizzling sound, like a potato slice being fried.
I try everything I can think of, but they won't respond.
Looks like the servers didn't just freeze – they went down altogether.
Akashi's nowhere to be seen, so I guess I have to ask Bremen. Hope she has some kind of solution.
Bremen, we've got a problem.
Hey, Commander. Having issues with the island base? Settle down and tell me about it.
The base's central servers are down. Hell, they're not only not responding, they also smell like something's burned.
Like something's burned? Sounds like the servers were pushed past their limit.
We need to fix them, stat. Or else the base's research, material production, and even communications will come to a stop!
Okay, and how do we do that?
Don't panic. They broke once before, and John fixed them. Apparently, the cause was that the condenser unit had completely fried.
Considering the recent calculation burden of doing research and how much it's been running, I think it's the same issue this time.
John told me how she did it. To completely repair a condenser unit of this scale, you need to replace the core components.
And to make the internals needed for those components, you need high-purity bauxite. Quite a lot of it, too.
Even the mine can't produce that much bauxite on short notice.
Don't worry about the bauxite. I'll figure it out somehow.
Do you have the time for that?
...Just be careful. Once you're done collecting, head right to the mine and find John. She'll have the tools and workspace to make the components.
John!
Oh, Commander. Here to buy some ore?
Sorry, but I can't help you right now. Bremen said the base's servers broke again. People are freaking out over there.
See, that's the thing. I've got the bauxite we need to repair them.
Whoa! Seriously?! One, two, three... This is more than enough! And it's pure!
Thank god you got here, Commander. Although, there's another problem – the parts I ordered earlier are still sitting in the harbor.
You're the only one I can ask, so... could you go there and look for them?
Alright. I'll head right to the cargo pier. You just focus on preparing the components for repair.
John, I found the parts! These are the ones, right?
Great! Yeah, that's the right model! Now I've got everything I need for the repairs!
Just need to finish assembling everything. I'll be done in a minute!

sequence: Sometime later...e later...

scripts.say: John, you done putting everything together?
Yup! Here it is – the condenser unit, the core of the servers' power system!
You just need to take this, replace all the burned-out parts, reconnect all the terminals, and in theory, they should be able to reboot!
Okay. I'll head back to the base and give it a shot.
You do that. See you around! Gimme a shout if anything else happens!
That's everything installed... Alright. Let's see if they work again.
Bwoosh...
The fans inside the server rack begin turning, going from slow to fast, producing the sound of a steady airflow.
Then, the little lights lining the whole rack's front turn on one by one until, eventually, the base is back in operation.
That's when something drops from the server rack – a piece of old paper about the size of my palm.
Hm? Where'd this paper come from?
Weird texture. It's hard... and strong. This is no ordinary paper. Is it treated leather, or some kind of special fiber?
Someone must've dropped it while doing maintenance, then it got caught between the racks, and the shaking set it loose. Anyway, I'll hold on to it.
Something on your mind, Am-Mer-Mar?
Commander... There's something I'd like to discuss.
Is it about the plans for the commercial area? Or is one of the stores having issues?
The former. The commercial area is meant to be a place to relax, yet it has little food on offer and lacks dishes that can draw people in.
If we don't improve this, it will negatively impact the vibrancy of the whole area.
I hear you. So we gotta expand the menu. I like the sound of that. You're good at planning and could come up with some new dishes, right?
Planning I can do, yes, but my expertise lies in management. To expand into a new field, I'll need to consult a professional.
Bremen at Café Manjuu is our local expert on the matter. If you could have a word with her...
Right. You want me to ask her for some tips on developing new dishes, I'm guessing?
Correct. As an initial idea, we should develop a healthy, tasty, and visually appealing dish that utilizes high-quality carrots from the fields and fresh eggs from the farm.
This will signal the availability of ingredients on the island and attract customers who desire freshness. However, we need to look further into precisely how we'll achieve this.
But please, Commander, go speak to Bremen and ask her for some tips!
Got it. I'll see what I can do.
Hey, Bremen.
Commander. Need something?
You guessed right. See, Am-Mer-Mar's got an idea. She wants to take the carrots and eggs grown on the island to make a new dish that'll be the jewel in the commercial area's crown.
So, she asked me to consult a food expert like you on how to develop new recipes.
Ah. Sounds like a classic good Am-Mer-Mar idea. Developing new dishes is indeed a science in and of itself... What do you want to know?
Good question... Where should she start? The right combination of ingredients? Finding a balanced flavor?
Ah, now that's an interesting topic. The key to creating new dishes lies in three elements.
Water, air, and fire?

Not those elements... The first is the element of understanding, as in understanding the ingredients you picked. For instance, carrots have a clear sweetness within their earthiness, while eggs have a mellow, warm fragrance.
The ingredients' characteristics together determine the flavor tones of your new dish.
Oh, I see. So, first you pick a base flavor.
Next, there's the element of balance. That sweetness in the carrot? You can enhance it by adding a little contrast in the form of honey.
You can also add a dash of cinnamon and nutmeg to give it depth. Then, for the egg, sprinkling some cheese for added saltiness brings out its aroma and tempers the sweetness.
Also, the flavor has to be three-dimensional. Saltiness, sweetness, savoriness, smell... Each of these has layers, and they all need to come together.
Makes sense.
Lastly, there's the element of appearance. We eat food with our eyes first of all, so your new dish has to not just TASTE good but also LOOK good.
Adding some enhancements to the finished product can not only improve the taste, but also catch the eyes of customers.
Gotcha. With these tips, I think even I could come up with a new dish.
Oh, really? Shall we put you to the test, then?
Me? I mean, I don't...
Doesn't hurt to try. Let's see you come up with a new recipe.
Alright. I'll give it a shot.
Whew... It's done, Bremen! I feel good about this one!
I have to agree. Looks appetizing, and the colors complement each other perfectly.
Mmh... This is fantastic!
Really?
Yeah. The carrots are nicely cooked, the slices are just the right size, and the sweetness is there but not overbearing.
And the egg – it's sublime. Cooked to just the right degree to lock in the moisture.
As for the cherry on top, the finishing touch of cheese, it perfectly balances the sweetness of the carrots, bringing the flavor of the whole dish together.
In terms of both looks and taste, I have no complaints with this carrot omelette as a signature dish!
Am-Mer-Mar will also surely love it!
Nice. I'll give this recipe to her, then.
Am-Mer-Mar, I came up with this carrot omelette based on your idea and with Bremen's guidance. Give it a taste.
Mmh... Its flavor is superb.
The simple sweetness of the carrots, the mellow fragrance of the eggs, and the saltiness of the cheese – it all strikes a sublime balance. Moreover, the texture is soft and the taste is rich.
This far exceeds my expectations. Yes, this is what the commercial area wants – a signature dish that embodies the taste of the island!
Glad to hear you love it. Bremen's tips for creating new dishes were really useful.
She gave you concrete tips?! If I may ask, could you share them with me?
Will... Will you tell me if I give you this?!
What's this?
Something I found between the pages of a recipe book.
Although it's incomplete, I thought it might be the fragment of a legendary recipe, so I decided to keep it safe.
Well, it's a fragment of something, alright.
Dunno what to do with it, but I'll take it.
What about... the tips?
Relax. I remember. I'll tell you everything she said with no omissions.
Bremen. Heard you were looking for me. What's up?
Thanks for coming, Commander. Are you, uh, familiar with the strange stuff that's been happening on the ranch?
Strange stuff on the ranch? Don't tell me Amerigo's animals ran off again.
Nothing like that, no. It's something more... creepy.
There's just been some trouble there, apparently. People hearing weird noises and such... Whispers abound that the place is haunted.
Haunted, eh? Now that's something I can't ignore.
I've got the gist. The farm is run by Homeric and Amerigo, right? I'll go ask them for details.
Be careful out there, Commander.
Howdy, Homeric.
Oh, C-Commander... G-good morning to you. Umm... Can I help you?
I was told that strange stuff's been happening around here lately. It's got the islanders worried.
It's true... S-some truly quite frightening things have been happening over the past few days.
As a result... the farm workers are too scared to go outside, and...
Take it easy, Homeric. Can you tell me specifically what's been going on?
O-of course... So, um, late at night, we've been hearing some metallic rattling coming from outside the farm.
It's not too loud, but it's quite clear, and it happens intermittently. It's downright terrifying...
One night, I-I just couldn't stand it, and I was worried it might be coming from thieves or wild animals, so... I mustered my courage, got a flashlight, and went out to look...
A-and then... when I got to the edge of the grassland... I saw a pair of glowing red eyes near the edge of the woods on the distant hillside!
Th-those eyes were staring... staring right at me, unflinchingly...
Thanks for explaining. Don't worry, I'll head there tonight and find out what those sounds and red eyes really were.
Th-thank you, Commander. Pl-please be careful!
Rattle... Rattle... Rattle...
There is a faint but certainly audible metallic sound coming from the woods in the quiet night.
They weren't kidding, huh.
The sound comes closer and closer until something emerges from the thick bushes ahead...
Moooo!
Moo Moo Cow? What the hell are you doing out here?
Did you break out to come munch on some grass? But then, what was that noise?
I notice the loose and damaged cowbell dangling from its neck, and I breathe a sigh.
So it's you... You're the "red-eyed monster" the girls saw, huh?
Well, I'd better go back and explain this to Homeric. This should be a relief for them.
Homeric, I've got news.
Commander... Did you find anything?
Yup. I figured out the cause. That metallic rattling you heard probably came from Moo Moo Cow's cowbell.
What? But... What about the red eyes I saw? Was that the cow as well?
Correct. The cowbell was a bit banged up and hung pretty loose, so that's why it sounded odd.
As for the red eyes, that was probably just the way the light reflected off of its eyes.
I suspect the cow was startled by a person suddenly showing up, so it froze in place and stared at you.
So, I worked myself up and got scared over nothing this whole time...
Well, now that we know what it was, we can get back to our work without fear.
Although... I'm not the only one who heard strange sounds. Amerigo said she heard them, too, and they were different from mine.
If you can, please go and speak to her. There might be something else going on at the ranch.
More strange sounds? Alright. I'll ask what that's about.
Amerigo...
Oh, Commander! Morning! Here to check on the ranch? Our Moo Moo Cow milk's been smelling delicious as of late!
Well, that might be because those cows are sneaking off the ranch to munch on some grass.
Whaaat? That can't be! I do a headcount every day, and it always adds up!
After they've finished eating and come back, yeah.
Seriously?! Why would they do that? I've been feeding them properly this whole time!
What's your process for feeding them?
Let's see... I take one, two, three handfuls of feed and just spread it around the ranch like this.
That's it?
I mean, yeah?
Then thank goodness this is a free-range ranch so the cows can go off and eat grass on their own.
You've got to feed them more than this. Cows have four stomachs to fill. You can't feed them the same way you feed sheep.
Ohh... No wonder they were so keen to go outside. It's 'cause they were hungry.
It's a good thing you noticed that, at least. Anyway, your feeding practices aren't what I came to talk about.
It's not? Then what is it?
People have been hearing weird noises coming from around the ranch.
Oh, that. Should've figured you'd heard about that.
Homeric told me. She said, in your case, the noises come from the toolshed, right?
Yeah, it's true! Although it's nothing like the rattling that she heard.
It's like this – when night rolls around, there's this banging noise that comes from around the toolshed, and it's extremely steady.
Can't be the sound of the wind through the trees, and it doesn't sound like rats scuttling around. It's so weird! I've gone there with a flashlight several times and found nothing each time.
Then I go back to my room, close the door, and just a short while later, it starts again! Bang, bang, bang, just like that!
It's almost like... it knows when I'm in my home, and that's when it starts banging against something!
I see. Thanks for telling me. I'll look into it.
I'll go there, have a look around, and see if I can't figure out what's going on.
Interesting... Freshly broken pieces of wood.
There's also a small pile of firewood in the corner. The cuts are recent.
An axe lying on the side. Signs of it being used not long ago.
This would explain the sound, but something doesn't fit.
Who's sneaking out here late at night to chop wood for Amerigo? A kind stranger who doesn't want to be known?
Or maybe... a sleepwalker? Whatever the case, I should report back to her.
Amerigo, I figured out the gist of what's happening.
Huh?! Y-you did? What's causing it?
The noises you've been hearing were someone chopping firewood.
There's actually a sizable pile of it lying in the shed.
You're telling me someone goes out, late at night, sneaks into my shed, and just... chops firewood?
That's the strangest thing I've ever heard. It being a ghost would make more sense.
Yeah, it's weird, but the evidence was there.
Come to think of it, when I chop firewood, the sound DOES sound pretty similar!
But who the heck's doing it?
I haven't figured that part out yet. At least we can rule out ghosts now.
True. That's a relief. Now I'm just wondering who'd do such a thing.
I've got a theory on that, actually. Although nobody in their right mind would do this, what if they were sleepwalking?
Now hang on, are you saying Olympic did this?
Could be. We should ask her. Maybe the reason she takes all those naps in the noon is because she does hard labor at night.
When you put it like that, yeah, I could see that! Let's go find her right now!
Olympic, wake up.
Mmh... Commander? What is it?
Was just wondering – have you heard any weird noises around the mill? Like the sound of someone chopping wood.
Mmh... No. I don't think so.
Okay, then have you felt any muscle pain or like your body's unusually heavy when you wake up?
You know, like you'd feel after working hard for the whole night.
Uhh... Not really. I sleep like a log every day.
I see. Have you noticed anything unusual or creepy, then?
Unusual... Maybe, yeah. This one night, I saw a figure with horns and no hands. It was a bit weird.
It was way past the farm, just wandering around.
I think I also heard some creepy laughter...
What then?
Then... I fell asleep. Zzz...
Doesn't sound like it's Olympic's doing. A figure with horns but no hands... This is getting more puzzling by the minute.
Guess I should have a look just outside the farm.
Odd. There're unusually many footprints in the ground here.
Hm? Hang on, these look familiar...
Nyahaha! My new and efficient patrol route is now complete, nya. I'll test the logging speed tomorrow, nya...
I hear something! Better go see what it is.
Wait... Is that...
You, Akashi?
Nya?! C-Commander?! What are you doing here, nya?
I should be asking that. Why are you sneaking around the farm with a notepad, huh?
I'm just, uh... making important observations, and... working out an efficient patrol route around the farm, nya!
Oh my god. It's you, isn't it? That figure Olympic saw skulking around.
Was it also you chopping wood in the middle of the night in Amerigo's shed?
Yep, nya! It was all me, nya!
What do you think, nya? Aren't I capable, nya? I worked out an optimal route around the farm and even did tests on wood-chopping efficiency, nya!
Why?
Why? Because I saw the animals were running free, nya! They're island assets, so we can't have them go missing, nya! That's why we need patrols, nya!
What was the point in the wood-chopping, then?
To quantify people's working efficiency, nya! You need data you can reference to see who's been slacking off, nya!
Aren't you pleased, nya? Aren't I just adorable and hardworking, nya?
Enough. You're gonna go to Amerigo and Homeric, explain what you did, and apologize.
Nya?! Wh-what for, nya?! I've just been trying to make people work more efficiently, nya!
I did it for THEIR sake, nya!
And you frightened people in the process, so good job.
Aww... Look, I'll give you this if you let me off the hook, nya!
What is it?
I found it during my nightly patrols, nya! No idea what it's for, but it makes my money sense tingle, nya. It's got to be some valuable treasure, nya!
You call this tattered piece of paper "treasure"?
You've got to trust my intuition, nya! Nice trading with you – bye-bye, nya!
What's the matter, Amerigo?
This is awful, Commander! My Baa Baa Sheep have gone missing!
Gone missing? When did that happen?
Like, a minute ago! I just went to get their feed, like I always do...
Then, when I got back, they were all gone! Every last one!
All that was left was a broken fence...
Calm down, Amerigo. They might've just gone a little farther.
Where do you usually bring them?
To the hill by the ranch! They love going there!
Okay, let's go check that place together. We might find some clues.
Is this the place? These bite marks are fresh. I'll bet it was the sheep.
Moreover, look at this dirt.
Oh! Are those hoofprints?
Yeah. While they're a little hidden by the grass, they were definitely made by sheep hooves.
Judging by where they were heading, I think they went into those woods.
Th-the woods? What are they doing there?
Let's find out. I can still make out the hoofprints clearly, so they can't have gone far.
You go back to the ranch and wait. For all we know, they might decide to go back soon.
Okay! I'll do as you say and wait there.
The hoofprints are even clearer over here. Quite concentrated in this area, too.
Must've decided on a direction and gone into the forest.
Around me, I hear the breeze and chirping birds – and, moreover, a slight rustling sound.
Is that them munching on grass?
Hoofprints are getting clearer and clearer, and so is the sound. The lost sheep must be around here.
Knew I'd find at least one here.
It seems to be fine. It probably just followed the grass as it ate and ended up here.
Now I have to bring it home. Need to be careful so I don't startle it.
I take out a fistful of sheep feed from the little bag I brought with me and slowly approach the sheep.

sequence: The sheep raised its head warily, but upon seeing it was you and the feed it so loves, it lowered its guard a bit and approached carefully.
At the right time, you took the rope you brought with it and skillfully tied a loop around its neck.

scripts.say: There. Good girl. Don't worry, I'll take you home.
Let's go see Amerigo.
Amerigo, look.
Thanks, Commander! You really saved my day!
You really gave me a fright, little sheep! You can't go off all on your own like that again!
I'm just glad it was okay. This sheep isn't the only missing one, though, is it? You said there were more.
Oh, yeah! There are more! They all went missing!
A big herd of sheep is hard to miss. Someone should've seen them.
By someone, you mean... Olympic and Homeric?
Yep. The fields are not far from here, and Homeric often watches the animals in the fields.
I'll go ask if she's happened to see any sheep.
Homeric, got a moment?
Hi, Commander. How can I help you?
Amerigo's herd of sheep has gone missing, and it's quite a big herd. Did you see any sheep earlier this afternoon or hear anything?
Oh, the sheep have gone missing? That doesn't sound like them...
The clock's ticking, Homeric. Can you tell me if you remember seeing them or not?
Goodness, sorry... Yes, I think I might have.
I think it was around... two hours ago? That's when I was measuring soil humidity in the fields to the east.
I'm fairly sure I heard some "baa's" somewhere in the distance. There were a lot of them, and they seemed pretty lively. They were heading...
Hmm. I can't remember exactly where it was, but I believe it came from the forest behind the farm.
So, that's where they went... I'll figure it out now that I know their general location. I'll go have a look!
Thanks, Homeric.
Of course. Take care!
Sure enough, here they are.
Quite a few of them, too.
Okay, that's enough free range time for you. Time to go home.
The last sheep...
Alright. It's following along.
Now to bring this herd back to Amerigo's ranch, where they belong.
Amerigo! I found all your sheep, every last one.
Really?! You've actually brought them all back?
Holy cow, you're amazing, Commander! How'd you find them?
Homeric spotted them, and she pointed me to where they were.
They'd had their fill by the time I found them, so it didn't take long to lead them back.
I think the reason they were so well-behaved was because you've always taken good care of them. They weren't reluctant to go home at all.
Of course I do! I treat them like family!
Whew... They all look fine! That's such a relief.
Yeah. I'm glad nothing bad came of them escaping.
That said, you really should reinforce the fences around the ranch.
It was just luck that everything turned out fine this time.
You're right! I'll go fetch my tools. I'll make sure the fences are fixed in place this time!
Good. Although, considering how big the ranch is, you'll need more wood to reinforce it all.
I'll go to the logging site and procure some for you.
Oh, thanks a bunch! Take care on your way there!
Amerigo, I brought the wood you need.
And I've got all the tools we'll need!
Great. Shall we get started?
Sure! Let's get to work!

sequence: Sometime later...

scripts.say: Amerigo, our wood supply's nearly out, but I just got done with my side!
Yup, I just finished mine, too!
Heh! Now the sheep can ram into these fences all day if they want, and they'll still never budge!
Thanks a bunch, Commander.
You found all my sheep and even helped me reinforce the fences. I don't think there'll be another breakout anytime soon!
Still, don't get careless. You should inspect the fences every day to be safe.
Yeah, yeah, I know!
Good. Go get yourself some rest. You've worked hard enough for a day.
Will do. See you later!
What's making that noise in here?
*sigh*... Never thought the outside world would be filled with so much darn noise.
Uh, good morning. Do you need help?
You sure are something, Commander – able to remain calm in the face of a stranger talking to you like this.
Seriously, though, there are way too many bees here for my liking...
Could I ask you to cleanly "deal with them" for me?
Any better?
I don't hear that nearby buzzing anymore, so...
Thanks, Commander. Ever so reliable. And you got it done so quickly, too.
I'll relish this peace and quiet.
Hello?
Oh, Commander. Here to hang out at the harbor?
I'd be careful if I were you. Bees have set up shop in this place, and they harass anyone who passes by.
If they're a problem, want me to help you?
Ugh... You know, I'm not supposed to rely on you for everything...
But since you brought it up, would you mind doing that for me?
It seems they're still making a ruckus somewhere around the harbor.
So I'd appreciate it if you could make things quiet again.
No problem.
No more noise now, right?
Yep. It's like all the noise in the harbor just went away.
You really have a knack for this, Commander.
Now I can relax for a while.
What's making noise this time?
Oh, I didn't realize you were at the farm...
As it so happens, the bees here are being a nuisance.
Here I thought I'd finally get my beauty sleep... Alas, I suppose that'll have to wait.
Want me to help you again?
Oh boy... I'm really making a bad habit of this.
Thank you for lending me a hand again. Next time, I promise I'll try to overcome it myself...
I've gotten rid of all the bee nests on the island now.
Lovely. It's as quiet as can be now.
The nights ahead will without a doubt be really peaceful.
Now I can get some sleep at last. And it's all thanks to you.
Thank you for always taking the time out of your day to help me.
I'm going to try my hardest from now on, so I can one day go out into the world...!
You called?
Umm...
Your gait sounds a bit heavy, but maybe that's just me...
Does the task of developing the island weigh heavily on you?
It does. Haven't gotten much sleep lately.
In that case, how about drinking some honey water? It has a relaxing effect.
Get some honey from the bee nests and bring it to Bremen at Café Manjuu.
She knows a honey water recipe that'll really soothe your soul.
Thanks for the tip. I'll ask her about it.
Anytime! I'll be praying that you sleep well tonight.
Bremen, could you...
What's that? Looking for a honey water recipe?
One time, long ago, I tasted the best honey water ever. You wouldn't believe how good it was.
I'll never forget that taste.
I did write the recipe for it down back then, but I've got no idea where it ended up.
Give me a minute. I'll look around the kitchen.

sequence: Sometime later...

scripts.say: Did you find the recipe?
Well, something hit me after a while of searching the kitchen from top to bottom.
I think I might've left that recipe in a secret place somewhere in the commercial area.
You... Hid it there? Not at home?
Yep. The recipe's special to me, and I'm more likely to lose it if I keep it at home.
Not sure I follow your logic.
At any rate, I can't leave the café for the moment. Sorry.
If you tell me where the recipe is, I can go looking for it instead.
Found it. This has gotta be the recipe Bremen hid.
And boy, did she hide it well...
That honey water must be out-of-this-world unbelievably good.
Bremen, I got your recipe.
Yeah! That's the one!
I can almost taste that honey water just from looking at this recipe again.
It's so good that I wish you could taste it right now.
Only problem is... I need fresh lemon, honey, and some rosemary.
As it so happens, my café's out of stock on those ingredients.
I mean, we should be able to find all those on the island.
Yep. If you can't find any, go hit up Am-Mer-Mar in the commercial area. She ought to know where you'll find 'em.
Hmm. All I'm missing is rosemary.
Doubt there's any of that on the island.
Got little choice but to go ask Am-Mer-Mar, then.
Hey, Am-Mer-Mar.
Ah, if it isn't you, Commander? Are you here to taste the area's delicious food?
Not this time. I'm looking for some rosemary. Know if there's any on the island?
Rosemary? What do you need that for?
Bremen's going to make some honey water for me. I'd love to try it, but the recipe needs rosemary.
One of Bremen's recipes? Now that does sound worth trying. Hmm... I see, I see.
The Golden Koi Restaurant should have some. They use it to season their food. Why don't you go look there?
Oh, the Golden Koi! Got it. I'll go check.
Is this rosemary? Looks like it.
Let's see... Fresh lemons, honey, and rosemary.
Alright, that's everything.
Time to see Bremen and have some of that special honey water.
Bremen, I'm back.
Found all the ingredients?
Ooh. They all look as fresh as can be.
The lemon looks refreshing, and the honey smells so rich.
And, of course, the rosemary looks to be in peak shape!
You know, I was a little worried you wouldn't pick the right ingredients...
Now it's clear you know your stuff, even when it comes to food!
I'll take it from here. You'll have the best honey water ever in just a minute!

sequence: Sometime later...

scripts.say: Hmm...
Hm?
W-well? Is it good?
Yeah. It's good alright.
Awesome!
Drop by if you ever feel worn out again. I'll prepare some more honey water for you then.
Thanks. Actually, could I have another glass?
I want the person who told me about the honey water to have a taste as well.
Sure, I've got some left. Here, take it.
Thanks, Bremen.
This is for you. Try it.
How fragrant... It smells sweet.
Did you make this honey water just for me?
Yeah. I wouldn't have known about this delicious drink if it weren't for you.
Just thought I'd share the final result with you.
Heheh. How kind of you.
So, uh... How do I give it to you?
Do I just leave it on top of the stone, or...?
No, no need to do that!
I hear a stressed voice from behind me.
Canteen?
After a short while, she appears from behind a tree.
Don't act like you didn't know what you were doing.
You used the honey water to try to lure me out.
Well, there aren't exactly many people who know about Bremen's secret recipes.
Oopsie. I suppose I should work on my disguises.
Anyway, I'll help myself to this honey water now.
By the way, if you want to discuss the "real deal" with me sometime, you're always welcome!
What're you drawing, Patrick?
Oh, hey, Commander! You showed up at just the right time.
I want to ask you for a favor. It's for a veeery important mission.
Let me guess – it's got to do with an island request, doesn't it?
Whoa! How'd you guess that? Your intuition is off the charts!
Reading the notes in your hand gives you a pretty good idea, that's all.
Anyway, where do I need to go and what do I need to do?
You have to find Stephen. She came up to me in a huge rush just earlier to give me a request. It must be something pretty urgent.
And, boy, I was just thinking, "If only I had more manpower," and that was when you showed up! You're our savior!
Praise be to our savior! Now take care of this urgent request, pretty please.
Stephen, did you drop an urgent request on Patrick?
It ended up in my hands, so I'm just wondering: What's the matter?
Oh! You accepted my request? Great! That means I'll make it in time.
Heheh – see, there was a little accident today.
I've been busy processing the recent surge in orders and haven't kept up with the cargo situation at the harbor, and, well...
There was this big bang, so I ran over to see what'd happened, and that's when I saw the containers used for packages in transit were broken!
Worse yet, I don't have any spares... I can order new ones, but it'd take quite a while before they arrive.
So, as a stopgap, I'm thinking we could make a few large wooden boxes. The problem is, I don't have the wood for it, and I can't just leave the harbor, either.
That's why I issued that urgent request to Patrick, hoping someone could go and collect the wood.
Alright, I've got it. Where should I go to find the wood?
Great! Go to the logging site. All the wood should be right there!
Thanks for the help, Commander!
Stephen, I've got your wood.
That's great, but there's another problem!
I was counting up the things we're supposed to ship today, and I noticed a pile of coal was missing from the storage!
I don't have time to look into why it's missing, I just need more coal!
Please, Commander! I'll pay extra on top of my previous request!
Where should I get the coal from?
The mine. It's not far from the logging site you were just at!
I just got back, and now I've gotta go out there again...
I'm sorry, but you're the only one I can count on! Without you, I dunno what I'll do...
Alright, alright. I'll go.
Hooray! Okay, I'll be waiting for your return!
I've got the coal, Stephen. Have a look and see if it's enough.
Whoa! You work so fast, Commander!
Let's see... Yep, that's more than enough!
Heehee – now there'll be no problems delivering all of today's orders.
And it's all thanks to you! Thank you so much!
Alright, then seeing as we've dealt with the problem, can I leave if there's nothing else?
Just one thing! Remember to tell Patrick you completed my request!
Patrick, I completed the request.
Welcome back, our savior! You really did everything Stephen asked for?
Yep. She even gave me a second request in the middle of it, and I had to go to the plains twice.
Whoa! You just started handling requests and you're already this fast and flawless. That's impressive!
Oh yeah, she also said she'd double my reward.
Don't you worry about that, I've got that logged!

Nya! That was faster than I– Nya? Commander?! Why are YOU handling my request, nya?!

Nya?! You heard about that, nya?

……Zzzz……
Olympic? Hello?
Zzzzz...

Every time I look at this place, I just feel so nice.

An iced coffee?

Get fresh ones, if you can.

Here you go. Juicy and just pulled out of the ground.
Don't be modest. Take as many as you need!
Bremen, I found the carrots you wanted.
Thanks, Commander!
The carrots Homeric grows really are a cut above the rest.

Fresh carrot juice, a dash of honey, and then...
Hmm. Should probably adjust this ratio a little more...
Now we mix everything together, aaand...
Done!
Looks good.

That's one basic energy blend complete!

Yeah, the diversity might be a bit lacking.

No. At the moment, I'm at a bit of a loss.

As much as I hate to burden you, would you mind gathering some opinions for me? It would help me tremendously if you could ask what kind of food or stores they'd like there to be.

Bremen! The commercial area's looking to add new stores, and Am-Mer-Mar asked me to gather some opinions from people.
What kind of stores do you want to see?

Clang!

Huh? Well, yes, that's true.

There is. I've laid it all out for you. It's mostly specialty products that are in season right now, so please have a look.
Peary, I got all the things you asked for.
Oh, Commander! The seasonal products are much more abundant than I expected.
To be frank, I was unsure at first if we could meet all the islanders' demands, given the limited variety.
Even if we couldn't, it's nothing to worry about. You went above and beyond, and that's what counts.
You flatter me. This was entirely thanks to you. All I did was sort the resources and make sure they were distributed properly.
Well, any good plan needs proper distribution.
On the topic of plans, if you ever get any more, just move ahead with them. When you need help, just give me the word.
Will do! Thank you, truly, for helping me so much.
I'll lay out my next plan carefully. I promise I won't let you down.
Peary? Are you... cooking?
Yes, I'm cooking... There is so much food, and I can't eat it all... Bleh... I don't want to see food for the rest of the week...
Well, uh, I heard the new development season is being prepped and should be ready soon, so...
"Being prepped"... "Should be ready soon"...
Ah, that's right... Akashi just the other day said our odds of smoothly developing the island were a mere 0.125%...
How did things get this bad...
Peary? Peary! (She is dispirited and unresponsive...)
Eek! C-Commander?!
S-sorry about that! I have my hands full with making all these preparations, and–
It's alright. Take it easy. Did something go wrong lately, and if so, what?
Well... I'll cut to the chase. A chain reaction of things went wrong one after another because I wasn't paying close enough attention.
There's a problem, we look into it, we start over, then there's a problem, we look into it, we start over... Rinse and repeat. Through some miracle, things have just about recovered now.
I see. I get the picture.
You do? That's great to hear! We're doing everything we can right now to make up for the remaining 87.5% worth of delays!
If you hadn't been here to help and support us, we would've probably given up halfway through...
Seriously, thank you, Commander. *sigh*... You being here has made the island a much better place.
So, what's left now? What problems are you dealing with?
Umm... There are no issues on the seasonal specialties front, and we've already got a detailed plan laid out...
Basically, um, everything seasonal will proceed as expected! Don't worry about that!
If you have a minute, then by all means, visit the new development area and experience what's new.
Nothing would encourage us more than if you could chat with some people and enjoy the beautiful sunrise and sunset!
You want me to just chill out? Is that it?
Yes, exactly that! Also, we caused you a load of trouble earlier, and for that, we're sorry!
But from now on, we'll work together to bring you a better experience of the development area!
Well, alright. You sure everything's gonna be fine?
Yes! Absolutely certain! Trust us on this!
What are you up to, Britain?
Meow?! Ah, it's you, Commander. I'm observing the fish, you see!
See that spot over there, with all those swimming fish? Aren't they beautiful?
Well, sure... I just get the feeling the glimmer in your eyes isn't because of how pretty they are.
*slurp*... Heheh... In truth, this is a fish hatchery! Naturally, a fish hatchery needs a lot of fish!
I'll let you in on a secret: There are actually a lot of fishing spots around the island. If I may-ow make a suggestion, do go and visit them!
Take my word for it: Your fishing bucket will be full before you know it!
Once you're finished, kindly release the fish into my hatchery. Be a dear and don't let me down, meow!
I dunno. I feel like someone's gotta eat them as soon as I release them there.
How rude! I'll have you know that I'm an expert when it comes to fishing. I can offer you advice on just about anything related to it, and I can even teach others how to fish.
Here, you may have this fishing rod! Go on and try it at a nearby fishing spot!
If you're unaccustomed to fishing, I shall gladly teach you about everything from casting to reeling.
Remember: Come back to me once you've got a large catch so we may release it into the hatchery!
Britain, I caught some fish.
Mee-ow! You only just picked up a fishing rod, and you've already caught such large fish!
Bravo, Commander! Bravo!
Let's see... We'd better record your first catch right meow!
Heehee. There we go! I've added the fish to your fishing collection!
Whenever you catch another fish in the future, I'll be sure to add it as well!
As you fill out your collection, you'll gain access to new kinds of fish to raise in the hatchery! And then...
And then?
And then you may admire the fish you've caught whenever you please! Quite thoughtful, no?
Appreciate it. I'll do what I can to diversify the hatchery.
Alright, let's have a look at your collection right meow! And don't worry about the fish you've caught – I shall take good care of them! Meow!
Peary, are you checking the development plan for the new season?
Umm... Oh! Y-yes, I am! I'm looking at it right now.
Thanks to your support of the island's development plans, I've even been able to comfortably establish a production schedule for seasonal produce.
As such, I've prepared a list of spring specialty products for... Oh, um! Sorry, just a moment...
Hmm. These prices are trending on the dangerous side... Either we cleanly cut our losses, or we watch how things go...
...Peary?
Oops! Sorry for keeping you waiting! As I was going to say...
We've newly added plans for aquaculture development as well. If you have any questions, feel free to ask Britain, our newest member.
She's the manager of the fish hatchery that was recently established on the island.
Speaking of her, she asked me for a favor just earlier. She wanted me to tell you to come check out the hatchery.
I've heard she's an expert on the subject of fish, from capturing to farming them. Please be sure to pay her a visit!
Oh, sorry, just give me a moment...
Hmm... This price looks decent. Maybe we should buy some more...
Peary? Hello? Peary?
Whuah?! S-so sorry! I got distracted again!
I was checking how much pearls were selling for.
The pearl market has been very lively lately, and I've even opened a trade business.
The only problem is that the price fluctuates in real time, so I tend to look at it a lot...
If it were you monitoring the ups and downs, I bet you wouldn't get flustered like I do.
If you're interested in trying it, I'll keep a trading channel open just for you. Let me know if you'd like to use it!
Peary, I hear you've been researching pearl trading lately.
Oh, Commander. Good timing.
Yes, I have. And I discovered a few rules as I did some digging.
What rules?
Have a look at this. It shows the price fluctuations over the last three months.
I've done regression analysis, trend forecasting, and also taken note of lunar phase changes and tidal data from this period.
And from where I stand, the price of pearls is about to go through the roof! Now is the best time to buy!
Are you sure? Market changes are pretty hard to predict.
This is a unique case, Commander. I'm using a new algorithm that takes 27 variables into consideration.
It's basically a guaranteed return on investment. Let me show you an example.
Umm... Well, there aren't any recently notable changes...
But my forecast says there should be at least a 15% increase within three days. We should buy 100 just as a test.
As soon as she makes the purchase, the chart on the screen suddenly starts moving – downward. The price comes crashing down like the water of the Niagara Falls.
Peary, the price is going down.
W-w-wait! D-don't panic! Th-th-th-the market is just making a technical adjustment!
You know, short-term fluctuations are a common thing. As my model shows...
As she continues talking, the market price falls even further.
Uhh... Don't you have some other business today, Commander? Like handling transports, or reviewing paperwork?
I'm in no rush to do those. I want to see how long this "technical adjustment" goes on for.
The thing is... my model's parameters could probably use a little more optimization.
What I'm trying to say is, you should just focus on other tasks! I'll conduct new analyses and find a way to recuperate this loss, I swear it!
Alright. Just give me a call if there's anything I can do.
Of course, I will! *sigh*... I really thought my algorithm was perfect...
Peary, how's the pearl trading gone? Did you manage to make your money back?
Make my money back? What are you talking about, Commander? I never lost any money to begin with.
You didn't? I remember the market price fell pretty rapidly just earlier.
That was just a temporary fluctuation. It happens all the time.
I didn't sell a single pearl, meaning I haven't lost money. You can't cut your losses if you haven't lost anything.
Are you sure you're not just coping?
It's not coping! This is my investment secret!
As long as I have the pearls, their physical value won't change.
All I need to do is hold on to them, then the price drops are just a numbers game.
And what if the price never returns no matter how much time passes?
It's just a matter of holding until it does.
Look here, Commander. The price has gone up since I bought the pearls, even if only slightly. I've not lost money, I've MADE money.
This is the appeal of long-term holding. Also, according to my now-optimized model, there's still room for further growth.
So you'll keep holding, regardless of if the price goes up or down?
Precisely. It's a safe bet. Why don't you give it a shot, too?
I think I'll just observe for now.
That's perfectly fine. Don't be afraid to speak to me whenever you do feel like investing.
Meanwhile, I'll continue looking for more secrets to make guaranteed profit.
岛屿·港口
亲爱的，终于见面啦。欢迎来到岛屿。
对了，听说明遇到了些难事需要麻烦指挥官呢。
具体是什么事呢。
我也不清楚，麻烦指挥官亲自去找她吧。
正在重新准备，请稍后……
Such nice weather... Let me... snooze for a little longer...
Hmm... There'll be a lot of shipments from the mine today, so I'll have to carefully manage our transport ships.
Building materials, tools, supplies – as long as you can find it in the harbor, I'll try my best to procure it.
I'm not tired, I'm alright. Simply seeing the seeds sprout, grow, and bear fruit is my reward.
Feeding 'em especially fresh grass makes their milk extra tasty. That's our hard work paying off right there!
Yep, just leave the iron ore here! The silver ore goes over there. Don't get 'em mixed up.
The quality of wood? Hehe, you got the right person! You got something nice to show me?
Greetings. I am Am-Mer-Mar, and I manage the commercial area.
Progress? Oh, right! Progress! To be specific, I think we're keeping up with the plan... probably... maybe... just barely.
Hello. Do you need assistance with a new exploration request?
Heehee – welcome to the orchard! Do you have any questions? I'm all ears.
Welcome. Care for a drink? Or how about an omelette? Here's the menu.
Welcome to the best party in the world! We've got tasty food, drinks, and rare treasure! I'm here if you ever need guidance!
欢迎来到最棒的集会！美食！美酒！奇珍！异宝！玛丽随时为你指路！
欢迎来到最棒的集会！美食！美酒！奇珍！异宝！玛丽随时为你指路！
The bees' favorite spot is the woods by the hills. It has loads of flowers, and it smells nice, and... Oh, wanna taste the honey?
My goods ain't cheap, y'know!
Is there anything I can assist with?
Meow... Commander, care to cultivate some fish? Should you have any questions, don't be afraid to inquire with me!

sequence: Wolf Unit
Flagship: Kursk
Objective: Scout the region

scripts.say: Halt.
I smell a beast... No, that's the stench of raw malice.
Yeah...! That aura's almost as strong as Gangut's vodka!
Up above! Dodge!
BOOOOOOOOOOOM!
Did someone just launch carrier-borne craft at me?! Geez, that scared me!
A carrier?! But that wave of attacks was too uncoordinated...
I see. Different forces ahead and behind us.
We're surrounded?
Two enemies total. One in front. One behind.
Hiryuu of the Sakura Empire... But she's only a Pawn.
The other feels... odd. That must be a META.
Recon drones would only be shot down. I'll use Flea this time.
F-Flea...?
A small submarine used for scouting. Perfect for intelligence operations.
You sure have a lot of crazy tricks up your sleeve...
But ol' battleship Sevastopol is still the real firepower of this operation!♪
...Sorry for not explaining ahead of time.
Forget all that. Why is a META working with a Pawn?
And Pawns shouldn't be able to slip through our radar undetected, right?
I'm afraid I don't know...
A second wave is coming! Watch out!
BOOOOOOOOOOOM!
She's strong... My attacks aren't even working.
At least the Pawn is like any other Pawn we know.
She might be a little durable, but she's a weakling otherwise!
Kursk, can we deal with this Pawn first?
I wouldn't. It smells like a trap.
More intuition, I'm guessing...
Right. Unlike you two, I have an especially keen intuition.
That would probably be why Soyuz allowed me to lead this unit. If that is a problem, I'm sor—
Don't apologize. You're our flagship, right?
Yeah! We'll do whatever it takes to help a friend of the revolution! Now, do we have any way to defeat them?
Absolutely not. We retreat.
Roger that! Wait... Retreat? Even though we finally caught them?!
I'll explain later. You said you'd help, right?
O-of course!

sequence: Fist Unit
Flagship: Sovetskaya Rossiya
Objective: Scout the Polar North Stronghold

scripts.say: The weather is getting really bad...
It only gets worse as we approach the Polar North.
This shouldn't be a Mirror Sea, but that meteorological anomaly weapon is just as troublesome. How does it even work...?
S-someone that looks like Omitter has been spotted to the northeast!
Did she use the snow and jamming to hide her approach?!
We're almost at the Polar North stronghold. There's no point in forcing ourselves to remain unseen anymore.
Concentrate your firepower and smash her to bits!
Confirmed the destruction of high-ranking Siren, Omitter! Ura!
She didn't fight like a high-ranking Siren. Was that one of those vessels I've heard about?
And the mass-produced Sirens here are a type I've never seen before. Rossiya, do you know them?
No... But I do know that these are much stronger than any other mass-produced ships we've fought.
Despite our defeating the elite humanoid enemy, their fleet has yet to fall into chaos. That must mean that the Command unit—
Another Omitter came out! This one doesn't seem like the real one, either!
Rossiya, our mass-produced ships have taken more losses than planned. Should we regroup first?
Not yet. We need to get a little closer to the stronghold! Ideally, we'd even draw the real Omitter to this battlefield!
If we're going to retreat, then it should wait until we have a better idea of their mass-produced ships' features! Hold on a little longer!
While distancing themselves from the enemy, the Fist unit attacked Omitter's vessel and gathered information on the hostile mass-produced ships.
Suddenly, there was a strong gust of wind that seemed to darken the sky all at once.
Is it just me, or is it darker now?
There was a biting chill as the blizzard intensified. In its midst appeared a figure darker than the sky itself.
A Sakura Empire carrier...?
For just an instant, Volga felt as though she'd been spirited away.
Her senses left the battlefield, returning to the Suliko that slept in the depths of the Arctic.
Shards of meteorite, the sample analysis device shining with an odd glow...
When her senses returned to the present, both the figure and the device had disappeared.
The communicator set up for this mission only buzzed, its signal blocked out by the interference of the raging blizzard.
Volga stumbled. Just as she was about to fall, somebody caught her and helped her back up.
Volga, are you okay?!
Did a Siren attack hit you?!
I-I'm fine! I was just a little distracted... Did you see that person just now?
A person? What do you mean?
All I know is that the sudden intensification of the snowstorm separated us from the rest of our unit and mass-produced ships.
Anyway, we shouldn't do anything crazy. I've set what few mass-produced ships we still have to patrol mode.
Who knows if they'll help, though? I just hope they can buy us some time...
The fleet is all separated... Oh, what do we do?
Watch out!
BOOOOOOOOOOOM!
A shell fired from behind landed dangerously close to the pair.
It came from behind us. Are we surrounded...?
D-did our mass-produced ships mistake us for the enemy?!
Umm... We're in danger, right?
Can't blame them... The Siren jamming is so strong, and this weather definitely isn't helping.
Rendezvous point... Contact... Coordinates...
That was Rossiya's voice! Thank goodness the communicator is working...
Phew... Oh! It's cool that the communicator is fixed, but look. The snow is thinning out, too.
Maybe the Weasel unit cleared their objective! Ugh, thank the stars for that...
This is Minsk. Volga and I have joined up again, and our communication line seems to be recovering! Please give us the coordinates of the rendezvous point!
This is Sovetskaya Rossiya. I've sent the coordinates.
Perhaps due to the weakening interference, Omitter's vessel has retreated for the time being.
We will continue the mission. Once we've all regathered, we resume our march toward the Polar North stronghold.
Roger that!
Everyone's okay!
Yeah! Let's go meet them right away!
My intel says the Iron Claw Demon's base lies in a part of the sea where candy appears out of nowhere, purin...
This sweet scent in the air... I've found it, purin!
KABOOOM!
An attack, purin?! Nice try, but I can block that easily, purin!
Huh? Wow, you're a lot stronger than the last one I fought.
Who are you?
Heheh! I am Prototype Bulin MKII, the Avatar of Gold, purin!
The Avatar of Gold, huh... I know you.
Gold has long been a symbol of greed and evil.
There was once someone claiming to be what you are, and she went on a rampage, turning candy into gold.
...I won't let you do that.
I'm taking you down, you golden fiend!
No! Gold is the embodiment of light, hope, and justice, purin!
YOU'RE obviously the bad guy here, purin!
Enough talk! Come down to me, Iron Claw Mechadrake!
Hah, "Steel Fists," purin? Is that what gives you your power, purin?
My Super Drill will make quick work of it, purin!
- Get her, Prototype Super Drill MKII, purin! - Give me a war cry, Iron Claw Mechadrake!
scripts.actorName: Prototype Bulin MKII & Iron Claw Demon

scripts.say: ROOOOOOAAAAARRRR!
A fierce battle unfolded. The Mechadrake suddenly brandished its iron claws and charged forward.
It happened so fast, the Prototype Super Drill MKII couldn't dodge, and was cleaved in two with just one attack.
What, purin?! An iron claw sweep, purin?!
Heheh! It's over for you!
I'm not surprised. This is the best your antiquated Gilded Age mech could do.
The Iron Claw Demon smirked, drunk on a sense of triumph.
But then...
Wasting not even a second to mourn the loss of her mech, the Bulin charged back into battle with a new mech.
Pierce the heavens once more, my Prototype Super Drill MKII!
What?! You have another?!
Hahaha! "Another," purin? What a naive fool you are, purin!
Obviously there wasn't just ONE Gilded Age mech, purin!
Indeed, the mech was of a mass-produced variety. The Iron Claw Demon was not expecting this.
She couldn't react in time to its golden laser, which reduced her Mechadrake into a pile of scrap.
NOW it's over, purin!
Victory is mine, purin!
Are you sure about that?
Then how come the results screen hasn't popped up yet?
Purin?! No, it can't be...
Come back to me, my second half – Iron Claw Mechadrake!
ROOOOOOAAAAARRRR!
Once again, the Mechadrake suddenly brandished its iron claws and charged forward, splitting the Prototype Super Drill MKII in half.
But then...
Wasting not even a second to mourn the loss of her mech, the Bulin charged back into battle with a new mech.
So stubborn...
Come back to me, my second half – Iron Claw Mechadrake!
The Iron Claw Demon cried out, and her iron beast was restored to full health!
ROOOOOOAAAAARRRR!
I'm done messing around with you, purin!
Prototype Super Drill MKII, pierce the heavens at triple speed, purin!
Another two golden mechs descended upon the battlefield.
The already fierce battle grew even fiercer.

sequence: The great battle between good and evil and gold and iron continued.
"Come back to me, my second half – Iron Claw Mechadrake!"
"ROOOOOOAAAAARRRR!"
Wasting not even a second to mourn the loss of her mech, the Bulin charged back into battle with a new mech.
"Come back to me, my second half – Iron Claw Mechadrake!"
"ROOOOOOAAAAARRRR!"
Wasting not even a second to mourn the loss of her mech, the Bulin charged back into battle with a new mech.
"Come back to me, my second half – Iron Claw Mechadrake!"
"ROOOOOOAAAAARRRR!"
And so the cycle repeated, continuing seemingly for eternity.
Only one will survive this ultimate showdown of ultimate destiny. Who will it be?
Find out in the next episode: "Prototype Bulin MKII Dies"!

The End

scripts.say: Our fleet follows the trail of wreckages for a while, when all of a sudden the fog clears, laying bare the Sleeping Sea's true appearance.
The debris and remnants of battle only grow more numerous, and the smell of gunpowder hangs heavily in the air.
Heh. Looks like we're catching up to her.
These remnants are very fresh! Sawai has to be around here!
BOOOM!
Just then, a yellow light goes off overhead – it's a signal flare.
A golden glow... The color of the Church's distress beacon.
It seems that Ganj-i-Sawai requests assistance.
Eh? Her ship is bloody massive. How could she get into trouble?
By being greatly outnumbered, or by getting into an unfavorable situation.
She is known in the Church not only for her great treasure, but also for being a priest of wind and rain.
They say that the Goddess graced her with the power to draw strength from these elements.
It is perhaps because of this strength that she was so confident in her own ability when we spoke.
Here, however, there is neither wind nor rainfall, and the accursed relic may even weaken the Goddess' blessing.
Given that, it's very possible that she has gotten herself into great trouble.
KABOOOM!
As we draw closer to where the flare shot up from, the sounds of fighting become very clear.
It's not long before we sight her – the girl who was so cocksure is now surrounded and taking a beating.
What do we do? Save her, or nab her?
Are you actually stupid?
We're gonna save her, duh! The LAST thing I want to do is draw the ire of the Church!
Plus, she'll be indebted to us if we help her!
This is a golden opportunity to earn a favour from the Church – and moreover, from a priest!
She'll be a HUGE force multiplier if we can convince her to join Tempesta!
São Martinho, you're with the navy, so you go in first! We don't wanna cause a misunderstanding now of all times!
The rest of you, get in formation and follow me!
KABOOOM!
Amidst the fierce fighting, the Great Royal Fortune suffers more than a few damages, as does the rest of Tempesta.
Even so, they emerge victorious in the end by working together.
Phew... A glorious victory!
My hull has taken damage... Need to patch it up, quick...
Oh dear... The cost of repairs will be eye-watering.
It's you, Tempesta and the treasure hunters... I'm glad to see you, for what it's worth.
Later, when you've tallied up the damage you suffered to save me, let me know how much it'll cost and I will compensate you in full.
Though she smiles, the confidence she had on our first encounter is gone, replaced entirely with sorrow.
(That's not the look of someone annoyed over a treasure hunt going poorly – it's the look of someone who's deeply anxious about something.)
(This is clearly more than just a hunt for a valuable relic to her.)
Do you fear for the Goddess' safety after witnessing such fearsome foes?
Yes... I do...
Her power must have waned such that she is unable to protect you out here. It's deplorable.
Will you tell us why you came here?
We may be able to help you.
*sigh*...
After a hesitant moment, Ganj-i-Sawai breathes a heavy sigh like she's letting her guard down.
I'm here on a confidential commission from the Church to investigate the strange happenings in this area.
My goal, as you suspect, is to retrieve the relic that can revive the dead.
I presented myself as a treasure-hunting rival when we first met, thinking working alone was going to be easier for me.
I pointed you to the Fountain of Youth for the same reason – that coming here alone seemed the better option.
Now, why are you here? Did you actually find a lead back at the Fountain?
Sending us on a wild-goose chase to get us away from you... So that's all it was.
Luckily for you, we caught that wild goose! The Commander found a lead which brought us here, and just in time to save you!
*sigh*...
Luckily indeed. Fate is a curious thing...
You think I'm a reckless fool for going into this sea all by myself, don't you?
I mean... Actually, no! You're not!
Royal Fortune quickly corrects herself, to which Ganj-i-Sawai lets out a snicker.
Truth be told, this is a secret holy site for the Church. You could almost say it's its back garden.
Come again?
Huh? Are you serious?!
Then it's no wonder why it's not recorded in any ancient literature.
You're telling me this weird place in the middle of nowhere is a holy site?
It is! This is the Sleeping Sea, the birthplace of the Goddess. Only high-ranking Church officials know of its existence.
People say that all these strange things have been happening because the Goddess' power is growing weaker.
Well, we did a lot of research and our attention finally landed on this place.
What we didn't expect was that this place had become overrun...
(From her phrasing, it sounds like she doesn't think we already knew this place was the Sleeping Sea, and that was why we came here.)
(I'd theorized that she somehow fed us the name and the map through Grimoire Terminal...)
(Unless she's feigning ignorance, we can rule out that possibility.)
(Why does it still feel like she's hiding something from us, though?)
(We would've gone to the Fountain of Youth regardless of if she told us to or not.)
(The fact that Terminal received a signal there would've happened irrespective of anything Sawai did.)
(Our reason for going there to begin with was to find a lead on the skelebeasts and the ghost fleet.)
(Of course, there was nothing linking them to the Fountain. It was just a Siren machine, now completely looted.)
(But, the monster and the fleet have appeared everywhere we go, from Whydah's hideout to this holy site...)
(The undead creatures and the concept of "immortality"... Perhaps there's more than meets the eye here.)
(What even is the Goddess? The deity of storms and the sea? Or is there more to her?)
(And why does the Church consider this place of all to be a holy site?)
(What if, like the Fountain of Youth, the Goddess is a machine of some kind?)
Sawai, what is the link between this site and the Goddess?
Sorry, who are you?
A-ha! Let me do the introductions!
This is none other than the founder and vice-leader of Tempesta! {playername}, the Commander!
Ahh, it's no wonder why you're asking insightful questions.
Normally, I wouldn't tell you a thing, much less allow you to come near a holy site.
However, you found and came to this place by yourselves, and you did rescue me as well.
Those things considered, I'm willing to tell you...
Assuming, of course, that you'll keep it a secret.
Simply put... this is where the Goddess lives.
Where she... lives?
Oh, perchance it's more apt to call it her "body." You see, the name of this place, the Sleeping Sea, refers to "the place in which Goddess sleeps".
I'll explain the rest at the temple that's here. Come with me!
If my theory is correct, the temple is where we'll find the answer to all these strange occurrences.
Fancy and I walk through a massive mechanical structure.
Our journey is smooth and unimpeded as the double doors slide open one after the next.
After passing through a corridor, we arrive at a vast, open place, as blue as the ocean.
A thin mist extends everywhere, and across it, I can see purple lights twinkling like little stars.
This is the Misty Pond.
I'm surprised... Even they have come back.
Come back? Who?
The lights. The silent souls.
They know we're here.
Then, great beasts appear among the mist, swimming across the surface.
Those silent souls... don't they look a lot like skelebeasts?
They are the essence of the skelebeasts as well as their source of power. It's how they move.
In fact, they are linked.
They must be running rampant on the outside for there to be this many of them.
So if they're linked, what will happen to the skelebeasts if we destroy them all?
They will lose their power and minds, becoming but empty husks. What they ought to be.
However, consuming all of them will take considerable time.
Do they taste like anything?
No. They taste neither good nor bad.
Want to try one?
Her tentacles start to squirm.
