Wasn't it supposed to be automatic? ...Did TB disable it and let us get jammed?
It's more probable that it simply wasn't automatic, or it failed. They did task us with testing TB's systems after all.
In a way, I'm relieved that her anti-jamming system failed. That means her coding is flawed, but flaws can be fixed.
Imagine if she worked perfectly all the time. Wouldn't that be a cause for concern? That could suggest the Sirens have a backdoor into her system and are saving it as an ace up their sleeve.
In that sense, yeah. When things work TOO smoothly, you get complacent, and that's how they get you.
...We're getting sidetracked! What about Ark Royal? Should we link up and assist her, or what?
Yeah, let's go! We can catch up with Cleveland's fleet later; Ark Royal needs help, and quick!
Hey, Cleveland! There's even more Siren wrecks here!
Really? Man... I would've stayed home if I'd known someone would do all our work for us.
Looks like they didn't dunk on just the Sirens, but all their facilities, too.
It's hard to say who did this, but it can't have been Ark Royal. The damage is just way too extensive to have been caused by her alone.
True that... What's even weirder is, she's not showing up on radar.
Let's look around a little more, maybe we'll find some answers! Be on your guards, guys!
Yikes, looks like someone had a real beef with this Siren device.
It's still burning, too... Whoever broke it, they must've been here very recently!
What's the purpose of this facility, anyway?
Beats me. Everything the Sirens get up to feels like 4D chess to me.
Doubt they'd give us a straight answer if we asked either...
Guys, check this out! I scavenged this off one of the Siren wrecks!
What is that? A crystal...?
It's no Siren tech, that's for sure! Do you think it might've belonged to Ark Royal?
I mean, maybe... But then how'd it end up in the hands of a Siren?
If I had to fathom a guess, they might actually have been trying to take it from her. That would explain why they were chasing her.
Sounds plausible, at least. But how does that tie into these wrecks? These are ancient Siren models...
...Cleve! I've got something on the radar! It's a fresh batch of Sirens!
We need to get in formation and– Wait... Huh?
Detecting tons of Sirens appearing at close range! ...But where are they?
We should have a clear visual on them! What's going on here?!
Seas are dead quiet, too. All signs point toward some kind of radar error.
Because if our radars were correct, we'd be surrounded on all sides...
One of the signals just moved! ...Through a structure, no less?! What the heck!
A-are we dealing with actual ghosts?! ...Do our cannons work against ghosts?
Relax. I'd sooner bet on radar interference or equipment malfunction.
Didn't TB send out some notification about Siren jamming just earlier?
If there's jamming going on, maybe that Ark Royal signal was just an error too.
Just as we think we've managed to engineer unjammable equipment, the Sirens show up and immediately prove us wrong...
Seeing as our radars have been compromised, we should probably assume our comms have been too, to some degree.
...Actually, I might be being overly paranoid. Let's focus on the facts: we haven't confirmed Ark Royal is here, but we DO know someone did attack this Siren facility.
The question is: who? Who's so powerful they can take out all these Sirens without even leaving a single trace that they were here?
No clue, but I wouldn't wanna make foes with them... Anyway, we should report our findings to the Commander.
While we're at, we should ask for new orders. We're kinda just speculating right now.
Everyone ready? Let's go find the Commander!
...What? Investigating the weather, of all things?
Yeah. Don't you remember? It's written in the operation documents. "Investigate the abnormal weather phenomena at the destroyed Siren Research Facility."
Cleveland's fleet took it upon themselves to do just that, from the sound of it.
No! Operation Siren is a united offensive against the Sirens! We're supposed to stick together, not divide our forces across vast distances!
The rest of the operation will be affected if you keep Cleveland's fleet there, doing dumb weather reconnaissance!
Furthermore, what if Ark Royal's signal and the destroyed Siren facilities are a trap meant to lure Cleveland's fleet in? That would put them in even graver danger than they are already.
You know, I actually agree. I think this directive isn't worth pursuing, at least not now. Essex? What do you think?
I think... it IS worth pursuing.
Sure, it might be a trap, but we need all the intel we can get for Operation Siren to be a success. That said...
They shouldn't be out there by themselves. We'll head there to back them up in just a while.
If Enterprise were in my shoes... that's probably what she would do!
System rebooting... Complete. Jamming has ceased. Wide-area scan revealed no abnormalities.
Look at that, TB is back online! All right, let's continue with securing this zone so we can come to Cleveland's aid at any time.
Numerous hostiles have been detected. Proceed with caution.
You sure? My recon planes in the air haven't spotted anything...
Update to data processing program required. Calculating time requirement...
Complete. This signal type will be treated as a form of Siren jamming. Reboot required to update definitions...
Complete. System jamming has been detected. Initiating anti-jamming program.
Is this the "ghost signal" Cleveland's fleet reported earlier? I'll admit, the things it does to the radar is pretty spooky...
Transferring interference pattern data to headquarters...
Error: Data package could not be sent. Connection with headquarters could not be established.
Connection to mainframe has been lost. Resuming in offline mode.
Dammit! Not again!
I apologize for the inconvenience.
I can't help but wonder: what are the Sirens trying to achieve with this jamming?
If it's meant to impede our progress, then there are more effective ways to do that... I'm almost inclined to believe they're just flaunting what they're capable of.
Essex, what do we do if we don't run into any Sirens soon?
Then we just reclaim the zone, simple as that. Whether we fight them now or later doesn't matter much, we'll run into Sirens sooner or later.
I will say though, it's bizarre that we've come this close to the center of the NA Ocean and hardly done any fighting at all.
Don't get me wrong, it's better than the alternative, but I'm worried that they might be amassing their forces somewhere...
...Anyway, let's get back to our objective: reclaiming the zone, then searching around for the source of this jamming.
Communications request received. Its sender could not be identified.
Hidden caller ID? I think we all know better than to answer that.
Sending a communications request out of nowhere and refusing to identify themselves... Sounds like the work of the Sirens' Omitter.
I agree. TB, deny the communications request.
Orders received. Incoming communications request has been rejected.
Brrzzzt...
You cannot reject me.
Hear my word, all you within this region. I am Arbiter. Lay down your arms and surrender. Resistance is futile.
Arbiter?! So you're with the Sirens, huh?
Sirens? I've heard of that name before... But I prefer to be known as "Antiochus."
Antiochus? The Ashes have used that word before...
In full, my name is Arbiter: Temperance ⅩⅣ. If you insist on titles, then call me by this one.
What a mouthful... You're the one jamming TB's systems, aren't you?!
Her anti-jamming measures were an amusing little puzzle. But I have had enough with puzzles.
This is your last warning. Lay down your arms and surrender. Resistance is futile.
Yeah, like we're going to do what some random voice over the radio tells us!
We're not surrendering to anyone! Now show yourself, "Arbiter"!
You're tired of puzzles, are you? Then come out and fight us on equal terms!
I offered you the easy way, and you rejected it. If I must beat you into submission, then I shall.
But... fight you on equal terms? Don't make me laugh. There is no fairness in war.
Sender has closed the communications channel.
TB, can you check the mainframe's database for info on Antiochus and this "Arbiter"?
Orders received. Mainframe database is unavailable in offline mode. Searching through local database...
No results found in local database. Attempting to reconnect with mainframe...
Connection could not be established due to electronic interference. Order could not be executed.
Warning: Multiple Siren signals have been detected.
Again? How long are they gonna keep messing with us like this?
No... This time, they're not messing around. Look, we have a visual on them.
Say what?! Do the Sirens have fricking optical camouflage now or something?!
Well... this disproves that whole theory about Mirror Seas being the only thing that can dimensionally displace organic matter.
Or maybe they've already formed a Mirror Sea around us...
In any case, we have to deal with these Sirens to secure the zone. Everyone, try to contact other fleets in the region and request backup!
...Not happening. Our signals aren't coming through due to Arbiter's jamming...
That doesn't leave us with much choice but to locate and destroy the jammer, then...!
I apologize for this...
It's not your fault, TB. Besides, it's not the first time we've been in this sort of situation.
We'll be fine, don't worry. Now let's show these Sirens what we're really made of!
A new type of Siren...!
It... seems to be an improved version of the Obstructor...!
Looks a lot stronger than the basic Sirens we've fought so far! Be careful, everyone!
My aircraft are performing at well below average because of all the electronic interference... Essex, should we retreat?
Not yet! Just keep a low altitude and make every bomb count! Agh, where are our battleships?! We need them!
KABOOOOM!
There they are! And thank goodness for it!
Essex! At last, we found you!
We came running as quick as we could after we got word from the Commander about jamming in the area. Had our own comms not been compromised, we would've arrived sooner!
Carriers fighting Sirens at close quarters... Novel. I like it.
If we could've kept our distance, we would've!
Of course. What's your status? Any injuries?
Our aircraft and weaponry are fine, but all our electronics are disabled and we're stuck here. You came right in the nick of time.
We're presumably dealing with an upgraded version of the Obstructor! Watch yourselves!
Don't you worry now. Us battleships can handle a jammin' without too much trouble.
We'll draw their fire. Carriers, fall back and try to provide support with your aircraft if you can.
Got it! We're counting on you!
It seems a lone Enforcer will not suffice. Then let us add another...
Temperance, we've found a clue as to Code G's whereabouts. It's time to stop playing around.
At last. Enforcer, disappear.
The Sirens... vanished.
Now I see. They have some combination of radar presence negation, optic camouflage, and some sort of tech that negates the waves caused by their movement.
If they've got all that, then it's no wonder we didn't detect them until they were right in our faces.
I remember Tester having access to optic camouflage as well, but that's not on the same scale as concealing an entire fleet of mass-produced units...
Jamming countermeasure has been devised. System will reboot momentarily. Do you wish to send a data log of your previous battle to the Commander?
Obviously, yes. Send it to naval headquarters too.
As it stands, we can't possibly defeat THOSE Sirens just by ourselves...
Hey... Am I imagining things, or did almost every Siren wreck just... disappear?
Huh... Now that you mention it, yeah.
Doesn't look like we'll get to gather many samples now...
We won't be able to analyze these new Siren models this way... The next time they attack, we'll be no wiser than we are now.
At the very least, we took a considerable amount of them out. I doubt they will attack us again right away.
Either way, we can't get careless. South Dakota, follow us to the planned spot for the Outpost.
Once we establish an Outpost and gain a foothold in this zone, we'll be able to repair our electronics. We just have to keep going until then.
Here it is, the place we're going to build the Outpost. We're getting pretty near the center of the NA Ocean now.
If we can also set up a supply base here, it should make it a lot easier to sustain an offensive on the Sirens' stronghold.
This isn't the only place we're building an Outpost, you know. Every faction is building their own in each sector surrounding the center.
Attacking from all directions? Now that's what I call a united offensive. The Sirens will crumble under the sheer firepower.
When we all attack at once, boy, it'll be the biggest sortie anyone's ever seen...
If we ALL would attack at once, we wouldn't need to first force the Sirens back.
As long as the Crimson Axis exists, we're reliant on the Commander bringing all the factions' ships together under the same banner.
That aside, as we get closer to establishing Outposts in each sector, there's still one big question with no answer in sight...
You mean the Ashes, correct? I believe the Commander's fleet ran into one of their members earlier.
They are, indeed, a mystery. I can't even fathom a guess as to why they're in the NA Ocean...
Naval command wanted to keep the existence of the Ashes a secret, but... well, that's not really possible with how much they make their presence known.
It's only a matter of time before they start considering ways to deal with them. Which, of course, will mean more paperwork for me...
Hang in there, Memphis... On another note, I've been thinking about something. Did you notice how we haven't been jammed since we fought off Arbiter's units?
What about it? Isn't that a good thing?
Well, yeah, but shortly after the jamming stopped, a regular Siren fleet turned up and engaged us.
And they weren't factory seconds either. They put up a decent fight.
Are you... saying that Arbiter's jamming affects ordinary Sirens too? Or maybe that Arbiter repaired whatever was causing disarray in the Sirens' chain of command?
I'm not sure which of those two is more accurate, but maybe the latter. The Sirens were sloppy ever since this operation began, and maybe Arbiter just fixed whatever was wrong.
Speculate in your spare time, you two! Focus! We still need to clear this zone of Sirens and establish the Outpost!
NA Ocean SW Sector - Outpost construction site
Hey, Saratoga, what are these ships? The transports for the materials and workers that will build the Outpost?
You got it! And don't forget the logistics team needed to sustain this operation! Which, by the way, yours truly is a member of!
Hey, I know what you all could use after all your hard work! Nice, cold ice cream!
I-ice cream? Why, thank you!
And that's not all you'll find at the Outpost! There's also a lounge area with entertainment, a cafeteria with snacks and drinks, and a recreation room to relax after a day of hard fighting!
Speaking of drinks, we've got some hot coffee for you as well. With or without sugar, Memphis?
Just hand me the cup, please. Knowing you, you'd add salt instead of sugar just as a prank.
Hey now, I wouldn't stoop THAT low! That's just mean! How about you, Essex? Want some coffee?
Yes, please.
Here you are! Now head to the provisionary dorm and get yourselves some rest.
The Outpost's facilities will receive an upgrade once the next stage of Operation Siren commences. Look forward to it!
The facilities we have now might be pretty basic, but as we reclaim more zones and establish supply routes, the resources available to us will increase!
...All that is to say, just have faith in me and the Commander!
Will do. Looking forward to seeing what the upgraded Outpost will be like!
That's the kind of enthusiasm I want to hear! Now, you must all be dead tired after fighting the Sirens for so long.
So just get comfy and have yourselves a rest while we await new orders!
East Méditerranée - International Canal
To think that there was a time when one could not access the Méditerranée through this canal...
Mm, it’s a bit of a miracle isn’t it? A supposedly neutral canal where anyone can pass through, regardless of their alliances.
What’s so unusual about that? Yukikaze the Great goes wherever she pleases anyway.
The situation here is rather complicated. Despite most of the ocean being hotly contested between various factions, this incredibly important canal is largely free from such power struggles.
Of course, this Canal has changed hands many times as a result of these geopolitical disputes.
If matters were left in the hands of the Iron Blood, Sardegna, and the Royal Navy, all-out war would’ve broken out.

With the Sirens’ appearance and the formation of the Azur Lane, the use and maintenance of this canal was converted into a public, international project. That has persisted even after the establishment of the Crimson Axis.
This canal arguably serves as a symbol of peace for humanity, and represents the joint front against the Sirens.
Of course, that makes it a rather unique case in this world. Once we pass this canal, though, I’m sure we’ll still see this conflict play out in full force.
So, what’s the state of the power struggle in the Méditerranée?
It’s a mess. Nominally, it’s under the control of the Vichya and the Iron Blood, but the Royal Navy has been expanding their influence.
Though Operation Siren has begun, the machinations of the leadership of the Azur Lane and the Crimson Axis ultimately will not change.
So that’s why you sent the 5th CarDiv the long way around...
(What... I thought that was just the usual course of crane bullying!)
Heh~ They’re our X-factor, so it’s only natural for them to arrive fashionably late. If we sailed our entire fleet through neutral waters, we’d be broadcasting our intentions to the whole world.
Besides, the Royal Navy’s leadership is going to be wary of us. Whatever they might have up their sleeves, we must have our own response.
Most importantly though, we’re in hostile waters. Draw too much attention to ourselves, and we might have to battle our way to Sardegna.
Akagi, are you truly in support of Operation Siren? After all, if the Eagle Union is going to be operating in the NA Ocean, the “Grey Ghost” won’t be...
An excellent question, Jintsuu.
I don’t mean to question your intentions, if you do not want to answer—
It’s not that complicated. The Sirens indeed are our common enemy, and the contents of the ceasefire agreement pose no detriment to the Sakura Empire.
We’ll continue our investigation of Siren technology while gathering information about the other factions.
But the most worthwhile prize of all... will be there as well.
Are you talking about the Commander?
...Ahem. There must be a deeper reason why the Sirens are suddenly retreating.
Bismarck and her cohorts did pass me a lot of valuable information, but... As you know, things are never quite as they seem when dealing with the Iron Blood.
Outsiders are outsiders after all. Nobody else will fight for the future of the Sakura Empire.
I shall reveal the secrets of this ocean with my own two hands~ Ahahaha...
Welcome to the Méditerranée, my lovely ladies. I am Littorio, from the Sardegna Empire. You must all be weary from your long journey~
It’s a pleasure to meet you. But I must ask, Littorio of Sardegna...
I was told that the Azur Lane would have representatives here at this negotiation, but why have I not seen them yet?
Did they have nobody to send here because they’re too focused on Operation Siren?
Maybe they’re too busy enjoying the splendors of Sardegna?~
To be frank, because the negotiations are taking place at a Crimson Axis-controlled port, I believe the point was to bring as few ships as possible, as to not incense the various leaders.
After all, we have just launched a historic attack against the Sirens, the collective enemy of humanity. Isn’t it only natural to seek a treaty that would put aside our differences?
Indeed, Littorio, it’s just as you say. This war will determine the factions that have the right to live.
The very essence, the beating heart of Siren technology will soon be laid bare before us. Is there any human selfless enough to forego such power?
About that... Well, it seems that the Queen of the Royal Navy is about to arrive. Perhaps that is a question you’d like to ask her personally.
An interesting suggestion. I’ll consider it.
And what about you, Littorio? Would the Sirens’ technology not bear rich fruit for the people of Sardegna?
We wish to reclaim our birthright, the Méditerranée, in its entirety. That’s the reason we’re still in the Crimson Axis.~
Heh, an understandable sentiment. But enough about us — let’s talk about the Sirens.
We came across quite a few Sirens on our way, as you may know. Weak as they were, what does Sardegna plan to do about this show of... negligence?
I always thought the Sirens had little interest in the Méditerranée. Have their plans changed recently?
I wouldn’t say that their plans have changed, but rather, the situation has changed.
The Méditerranée is naturally well-protected, making a large-scale Siren invasion extremely difficult as long as the points of entry are guarded.
As for the ones responsible for this defense, from the perspective of the Royal Navy, they are in charge of defending the western entrance while Sardegna is in charge of the east.
Since the announcement of Operation Siren, the Royal Navy’s fleets have thinned out, allowing more stray Sirens through.
As a sign of goodwill, the Royal Navy lifted their blockade - but in that process, also let more Sirens through.
Of course, there is little to be worried about. I have personally formed a fleet to eliminate the stragglers, as they are not welcome in these waters.
But let us tarry here no longer, my beautiful Signorinas. The fine wine and delicacies of Taranto await.
Behold, the wondrous port of Taranto. ...Ah, did the Royal Navy arrive before us?
My sincerest apologies for being absent to greet Her Majesty’s arrival.
There’s no need for formalities. I know the Méditerranée like the back of my hand, and I could easily sail to Taranto blindfolded.
I see... You don’t look like you came from sightseeing though. Did something happen on the way?
Oh, nothing out of the ordinary. Just the usual stuff with the Crimson Axis ports not allowing me to enter. It definitely wasn’t a waste of my time at all.
I am sorry to hear that. Even for a purpose that is supposed to transcend allegiances and factions, to think that there still are those who will not open their ports...
I see the Sakura Empire is here as well. Will Akagi be the representative?
(Well, Akagi would be the one negotiating even if Nagato was here. I must say, I was hoping to see Yamato though...)
Good day, Akagi. Have the leaders of the Sakura Empire given you full authority to conduct these negotiations?
Hmm... I seem to hear someone calling my name, but...
Oh, it’s the little queen of the Royal Navy. I apologize for not noticing you given your... stature, Your Majesty.
As for the question you asked earlier... surely the Royal Navy’s intelligence-gathering capabilities have not sunk to such pitiable levels if we are to take on the Sirens.
Why you...!

Our resources have indeed been a bit strained... but we will rectify our shortcomings. Perhaps we should consult the Eagle Union, since you said that about them as well before the events of Operation AF.
Heh, you...
Now now, everyone, let’s calm down~ We’re all here for the sake of peace, so why don’t we set this aside for now?
We’ll begin the negotiations when the Iron Blood arrives. Until then, please enjoy everything Taranto has to offer.~
Sister, are you just going to leave Taranto like that?
We’ve already finished what we came for. Besides, who knows how long we’ll be stuck here if we get caught up with that crowd...
(It wasn’t easy to successfully forge a treaty, but we’ll lose sight of our original purpose if we stay here too long...)
(Wine, food, and endless merriment... does Sardegna not even realize that we’re in a race against time?)
It seems like Sardegna doesn’t want to get their hands dirty. Are they not planning to do anything unless war comes to their doorsteps?
...In any case, we’ve finished resupplying and the treaty’s been signed. There will be plenty of time for celebrations once Operation Siren is over.
I think that scary lady from the Iron Blood was going to spend some extra time at Sardegna... Do all those people have no sense of urgency...?

Though this was my first time dealing with her face-to-face, I could tell from a glance exactly what kind of person she is. Though she seems to be sitting around, she’s always planning three or four steps ahead.
(I’m sure she’s planning to make her next move while everyone’s attention is focused on the NA Ocean.)
(There’s no telling what that person is thinking. We’re not negotiating on our turf here, and there’s no way we’d be able to get away with those kinds of tactics.)
(I’m glad I sent the 5th CarDiv out after us. We’ve come too far to go back home empty-handed.)
Did you notice that Queen Elizabeth was even in more of a hurry to leave than we were?
They seemed very troubled by Tirpitz’s sudden appearance in the NA Ocean... In any case, that also gave us an opportunity to leave as well.
Everyone seems to be looking for something... Do we even know for sure that it’s there?
Are you doubting my information?
No, of course not... Are we going to head into the NA Ocean as well then?
No, we need to make a visit to the Vichya Dominon’s port of Dakar first.
After all, I’m dying to find out about the “present” the Iron Blood prepared for us. Ahaha...
Is that Dakar up ahead? I heard that this one of the Vichya Dominion’s most important ports, but it looks rather deserted...
That’s true. I don’t see any ships here from either the Vichya or the Iron Blood.
Or rather, I shouldn’t say that there aren’t any. I think that’s destroyer coming towards us is a messenger from the Iron Blood.
Welcome to Dakar. I am the destroyer, Z2, and I have been assigned to wait for your arrival.
Huh? You’re our entire welcoming committee?
Yes, I’m the only one here right now at Dakar. But, you’re not here to inspect the Iron Blood fleet, are you?
Let’s talk business. This way, please.
That’s the Iron Blood efficiency I want to see.
Woah, is this an Iron Blood research lab? Now this piques my interest!
I see, this is a more reductionist view of the Wisdom Cube. Purely empirical, unlike the more metaphysical approach we take in our research.
(A modular, large-scale dock. Energy absorption devices. Adaptive bioengineered rigging. Communication equipment resistant to EM attacks. Even “imitations” of Mirror Seas...)
Yuubari, do you think there’s anything here you’d be able to use?
You bet! I have plenty of ideas I’m dying to try out as soon as we get back!
(The Iron Blood seems to have successfully extracted much from the Sirens... But us, on the other hand...)
(Nay... If there’s something you want, you must seize it yourself...)
The Iron Blood doesn’t seem to be coming. Is this their idea of a joint operation?
I’m not sure exactly what Friedrich is planning, but our main fleet has also moved to the NA Ocean. If everyone’s operating in the same area, doesn’t that technically qualify as a joint operation?
Where’s your main fleet then, and what are they doing?
I’m sorry, but I’m not privy to that information. I’m just a destroyer who was told to stay behind.
If Prinz Eugen was here, I’m sure she’d know something...
Otherwise, I would go ask Friedrich directly. She should still be staying behind in Sardegna.
...We just left Taranto. Are you saying we should just turn back?
Ah, sorry, you can just use the communicator. That should do just fine.

It’s fine, there’s no need for that. The Sakura Empire has more than enough power to complete this operation. If you’re not willing to cooperate with us, your actions are also of little concern to us.
We will head out when our ships are resupplied.
Very well, I’ll start making the arrangements. Are you sure you want to leave so soon though? We scheduled a demonstration of some our technology tomorrow...
We appreciate the sentiment, but time is of the essence. Yuubari, if there’s anything you’d like to see here, you’re welcome to stay behind.
I’m sorry I could not meet your expectations.
Let me try to get in contact with Bismark or Friedrich first. I’ll try to let you know if they share any information about where our main fleet is.
If you’d like, please take this cutting-edge Iron Blood communication device with you.
This device should have higher resistance to the Sirens’ jamming attacks, so I hope you will find it useful.
Will this be able to counteract the jamming effect of the Mirror Seas?
And just to make sure, you have no objections to us bringing this back to the Sakura Empire, right?
Correct, it’s yours to keep. Consider it our gift.
Thank you very much.
No problem. Please follow me to the resupply and maintenance area.
Look at how these enemies crumble before Yukikaze the Great!
The Sirens here are much weaker than what the data suggested.
Yes, their lack of resistance is almost uncanny. If they’re consolidating their forces in one area, one would expect a tougher fight, yet we’ve already taken back so much territory.
Yeah, there’s even a big red danger mark on the map here. What gives?
Heh, I get it now! My luck has once again made the enemy completely miss us!~
That may be true... but we’ve never seen so many Siren research facilities packed so densely together before.
And because this zone lies just outside the Azur Lane’s operation range, these facilities are largely intact still. We truly did luck out this time.
Indeed. Yuubari, collect a Siren sample to bring back home. Once we get back to the Sakura Empire, you can experiment with it as much as you’d like.
Make it quick though. There are greater rewards waiting for us ahead.
Akagi, don’t you think we’ve rushed in a bit too deep?
We haven’t encountered significant resistance from the Sirens yet, but the intensity of their counterattacks is gradually increasing.

If this trend continues, we can expect to run into a large Siren defensive force ahead. Even the Azur Lane has stopped pushing forward and is now focusing on establishing forward bases. Should we wait for the 5th CarDiv before continuing?
No, we press forth precisely because the Azur Lane has stopped attacking. As I said, this is a race against time.
Even if the enemies are a bit tougher, it’s nothing we can’t handle. We haven’t even encountered a Mirror Sea so far.
What sets us apart from the Azur Lane is our decisiveness. No risk, no reward. Those who are afraid to take the initiative will also see their opportunities snatched away.
Point taken, but how about contacting them at least? Why not decide on a point of attack, and have them cooperate with our advance?
Once we join up, we’ll be able to push even farther into Siren territory.
So be it. If they are worthy of their names, they will be here anyway.
Very well, I’ll get in touch with them.
All units, stay in formation and advance!
...Eh? Where’d all this fog come from?
We’d be lucky if it was just that simple. Any sudden environmental change while we’re in Siren-controlled waters should be considered an anomaly. Stay vigilant, everyone.
Ugh... My navigation instruments are spinning around like crazy and all the readings are going haywire... Akagi, we’re getting jammed!
BZZT————ZZZZZZZ——————
Hwuh?! Why’d the communicator start screeching?!
Someone’s trying to say something... But I can’t make it out through all the static...
Even the anti-jamming communicator we got from the Iron Blood is acting up... Is it really impossible to overcome the Siren interference?
Also, what’s this voice-like noise coming from the communicator? I really need to tinker this thing around thoroughly...
Anomalous weather and jammed communications... I’m afraid we’ve wandered into a Mirror Sea. Sooner or later, an armada of Sirens is going to show up.
Sister, the situational clearly is abnormal. We should slow down and survey the situation first... Sister?
This fog... Could it be......?
Akagi, what’s happening to you?
Ah, sorry, I got lost in my thoughts. What were you saying?
....Kaga? Where are you?
Kaga? Jintsuu?! ...Yuubari! Yukikaze!
...What in the world just happened...?
The smell of gunpowder in the air... I’ve been here before... Mid...way...?
Yes... Yes... It is! I remember, this is Operation AF! That Grey Ghost is here!
Damnit... Had it not been for you, the Eagle Union would have been powerless to stop us in the Pacific... It’s all your fault, Grey Ghost...!
Because of you... I, Akagi... was ignobly defeated...
Soryuu... Hiryuu... Kaga... Even the memories of my sister...
It’s your fault... You took everything from me...
I won’t forgive you... I’ll never forgive you... Grey Ghost! Damn you...!
You still remember me. I’m honored.
That was a damn exciting battle! Your leadership was top notch!~
Indeed. You still want to take your revenge on us, right? Then come and fight us, forevermore.
Even after you returned, you seemed to blame everything on the Five Minutes of Fate. But given five days, five years, five eternities... What could you possibly do?
You cannot escape fate... the fate engraved upon your hull. Fate is not so fragile, unlike that little amulet your sister gave you~
Shut up! Shut up! You’ve all come before me to die... And I’ve been waiting to send you all to hell! Ahahahaha!!
Come, Akagi... This time, nobody will keep you from your revenge. Not the Sirens. Not the Sakura Empire. Not the Eagle Union. And not Amagi.
I’ll run you through for underestimating me, Grey Ghost! My entire life, I’ve lived for this moment... The chance to sink you myself!
The strong devour the weak... The fit survive... Such is the nature of... this...
—————That voice... Shoukaku... Zuikaku...?
Akagi! Yuubari! Jintsuu! Yukikaze! Where are you?!
(Impossible... How did everyone just disappear? But, I should consider myself lucky for not getting attacked...)
(It’s impossible for me to operate my aircraft in this thick fog...)
(Wait... This weightiness... I’m... no longer an aircraft carrier...?)
It’s been a while, Kaga. It seems like you’ve finally grown up, strong enough to sail the seas with the Sakura fleet.
A...magi...?
How is my little sister doing? I trust that you’ve been taking good care of her like I asked?
Right now, she’s...
Gone? That’s right, I should have been the one to be at her side. Not you.
Ah, how I regret the decision I made back then. Look what has happened to my Akagi, to my Sakura Empire. All because of you, Kaga...
Because of... me...?
I’m disappointed in you, Kaga.
If I destroy you here, I’ll be able to see my sister again.
What happened to the proud and mighty Kaga I once knew? Are those guns you carry just for show?
...Don’t mess with me, Siren! Amagi would never say these kinds of things! I have no idea who you are, but you’re going to shut your mouth!
Graahhhhh!!
Ehhh?! Kaga?! Why’d you suddenly start shooting at me?
Woah, that was close. Good thing I didn’t run up any closer...
Huh? Zuikaku...?
Amagi... Where’d Amagi go? I was just firing at her...
Firing... No, that can’t be... It’s been ages since I became a carrier. And Amagi, she’s already... What’s going on?
What’s going on?! That’s supposed to be my line!
When you entered this area, you suddenly got caught up in a Mirror Sea. We tried calling out to you, but that’s when you attacked us!
I know you don’t like us, but luring us out here to get rid of us in an “accident” is a really unfunny joke, Kaga~
That hurts, Shoukaku... More importantly, did you find the others?
We rushed over after Jintsuu used her foxfires to call out to us.
However, when we arrived, we found the entire ocean surface coated with this thick fog.
I started getting a bad, bad feeling about that fog as soon as I heard about it.
I wasn’t sure if I wanted to head in, and that’s when I saw Yukikaze coming out!
Yukikaze, you managed to escape from the fog by yourself...?
Yukikaze the Great has no idea what happened either! I was just sailing about when everyone suddenly vanished into the fog!
I went around looking for everyone, and next thing you know, I was out of the fog and right there in front of Yamashiro and Shoukaku’s fleet.
We decided to wait outside at first, but nobody else was leaving the fog.
At that point, we had no choice but to head in to look for everyone... and that’s when we ran into you.
...I’m truly sorry. I let myself be deceived by the Sirens’ illusions... Or rather, I still haven’t managed to sort through my own memories all this time....
So basically, everyone covered by this fog is showed some kind of illusion as if they’re trapped in a dream? What do you think, Kongou?
That, coupled with the jamming effect, basically confirms that this is no natural phenomenon.
We haven’t been affected so far, but that’s not to say we won’t get attacked if we stay too long. Let’s rescue the others as fast as we can.
Crap...! I just realized, what if the others are going through the same thing Kaga was? We have to find them quickly!
Thanks for rescuing me... According to my research, this sea fog definitely has a hallucinogenic component, which is responsible for giving us illusions.
As for why it didn’t affect Yukikaze... Maybe she was lucky enough to get out of it before it could affect her. Or maybe she doesn’t have enough going on in her head for the Sirens to toy with...
I definitely will have to look into this further...
Calm down, Yuubari! You only just came out of your hallucination, so rest up first!
Look up ahead, it’s Jintsuu! Yukikaze the Great is coming to rescue you!
Safety first, Yukikaze! She might start attacking because of her hallucinations just like Kaga.
Heheh~ Just leave it to me!
...No, we shouldn’t talk of this plan any more. All we need to do is to focus and charge forward.
I can’t accept that. I can’t do something like that.
I’m honored to hear you say that, but...
...She doesn’t seem any different to me... W-woah, those flames definitely aren’t normal!
They’re definitely going to come after me if I get too close... So, I’ll land the first blow!
Wait, wait... What am I going to do if I accidentally hit Jintsuu?
Maybe I’ll aim a bit to the side then... Hmm, maybe I should just call out to her with a loudspeaker or something...
What about a signal flare? ...That’s probably out. Wouldn’t want the Sirens to gather around here...
All right, I’ll go with the first plan! Loudspeaker it is!
...Yukikaze, what are you doing here alone?
J-Jintsuu! Y-you’re back to normal?!
So everything that happened was an illusion after all... Ugh, my head hurts... Why are you the only one here? Where are the others?
We’ve found everyone except Akagi! Let’s head back and look for her together!
That’s Akagi over there, isn’t it? I can’t see clearly from this distance though...
No, that’s definitely Akagi all right. Nobody else would bomb the empty sea surface repeatedly while cackling maniacally.
...I wonder if I was also like that...
Well, y’know...
How disgraceful...
Eh? Look, there’s someone else next to Akagi!
But Akagi doesn’t even seem to notice...
That rigging... is that a Siren?!
It must be. But we’ve never seen any Siren like that before...
As far as I can tell, it’s just observing rather than trying to attack...
This whole thing feels surreal...
Ahaha... Do you think so too?
Woah! It’s speaking directly into my head?! Does anyone else hear that?!
I think it’s using vibrations in the particles of water in the sea fog to communicate....
That Siren must be the one behind the creation of this Mirror Sea!
I do know one thing for certain though. We’re going to have to defeat that Siren if we want to rescue Akagi...
Let’s get moving then. Shoukaku, Kaga, attack the Siren with me draw its attention away. Yukikaze, Jintsuu, bring Akagi back safely!
Are you fine with that, Kaga?
No objections. Prepare for combat - we have no room for error.
I don’t think I’m landing a single hit... Zuikaku, what about you?
Same here, sis! Just when my torpedoes and bombs are about to hit, it’s as if there’s something else in the way!
Everyone, Akagi’s starting to wake up! Zuikaku, Shoukaku, fall back! We’ll take this fight another time!
Damnit... This Siren’s going to burn... for making a fool out of me!!
Akagi, look... The Siren’s already gone.
Did it decide to retreat...?
The fog isn’t receding though. If anything, it’s getting even thicker. We have to get out of here quickly.
Yukikaze, do you still remember the direction you went in to leave this—
Woahhhh!! Everyone, there’s another Siren over here!
Akagi... We can’t advance any further... We need to pull back!
This is a reminder as to why the Sirens are so dangerous... They’ll never allow themselves to be pawns in your plans.
We’re almost there... If we work together, then...
I refuse, Akagi.
We used up all our ammo back there fighting the other Siren. There’s no way we’d be able to deal with all the enemies that lurk ahead.
Besides, there’s something else about this fog... Look, it’s already happening. You can feel the fog eating into your rigging, can’t you?
Yuubari just told me, this fog also has corrosive qualities!
We’re going to get annihilated at this rate, Akagi. We already got the Siren sample we came for, so let’s head back to Dakar.
Live to fight another day, huh? Sister, Zuikaku is right.
Very well... Turn back and head towards Dakar... But heed my words, Siren, we’ll be back!

sequence: The azure horn sounds across the ocean.
To which the crimson shadow dances deliriously.
Four blades point towards darkness, lit by ember and ash.
Who programs those who arbitrate beneath the maelstrom of secrecy?
For all that the surface conceals shall be laid before the abyss.
→To Be Continued

scripts.say: The maritime outpost at the forefront of Operation Siren, a major counter-offensive to eliminate Siren activity in the NA Ocean, has been quiet lately.
Ten days have passed, but the next phase of the large-scale assault has not started yet.
The only things on the calendar are meetings, meetings, and more meetings.
Though the Eagle Union's fleet is assembled and stands ready, the green light has not been given to continue the large-scale assault, and the operation's progress has slowed down considerably.
As anyone who has studied the art of war knows... it is rarely a good idea to lose the initiative when on the attack.
Eagle Union Outpost - 10 days earlier
(Alarms blaring)
I was looking over some reports in the office when the sound of sirens blaring ripped through the air.
Sorry for bothering you this late, Commander. Are you still working?
I was fine-tuning the details for the upcoming large-scale assault. As the commander, it is my responsibility to see the operation through to completion.
Earlier, there was a report that an anomalous phenomenon was seen from the maelstrom in the middle of the NA Ocean.
Here's the intel that our recon team put together for us. I thought you should look over it as soon as possible.
"...A large cluster of Siren facilities has been seen around the maelstrom. The facilities may directly be linked to the weather abnormalities..."
I initially also tried to send some recons out to survey the situation, but my planes were shot down before they could gather any information.
The fact that the Sirens have erected an entire complex of facilities while also not revealing their main forces is a reason for concern.
The extent of the activity we're seeing goes beyond what we predicted.
"Were they poised to attack you?"
Not yet. Just to be safe though, I raised the threat level and gathered the main fleet.
"I have to meet with the Naval HQ about this. We must make preparations to face the Siren stronghold."
Of course. By the way, there was also another emergency message from the Naval HQ. I originally was coming to let you know about it.
It may be about the same thing we're talking about, but I'm getting the hunch that there might be a lot more to it.
We'll find out. Regardless, the Naval HQ should be taking any measures necessary to combat this anomaly.
"While I'm busy, you're in charge of defending the base, as well as collecting any information you can."
Understood. I'll take command of the fleets patrolling the base. I'll make sure you're able to complete your work without being disturbed.
I sighed to myself, knowing that everything I had been working on was just about to go out the window.
I knew there would be a drawn-out debate among the higher-ups at Naval HQ, but I didn't think it'd end like this...

Two approaches have been hotly debated: the first, launching a focused assault to break through the Sirens' defensive line, and the second, slowly whittling their forces down until we have them surrounded.
What's more, some are requesting our capital ships be withdrawn and reassigned to do Siren research missions instead.
Either way, we have too little intel to determine our best course of action... Hopefully, tomorrow, we will.
I see Memphis and Sheffield are here.
From what I've heard, Sheffield is joining us per secret orders from Queen Elizabeth herself.
They're in the middle of a conversation. Let's not disturb them.
Oh, Commander? There you are.
Well, she saw me. I might as well talk to them and hear what's up.
I leave the matter in your hands. Now if you'll excuse me...
...Ah. It's good to see you, Master. I hope you've been well.
Please try not to lose any sleep over Naval HQ's indecisiveness. For now, I suggest clearing your mind and getting some rest. I must go now. Farewell.
Sheffield bowed to me, then left quite abruptly after offering her... advice.
Working hard as always, Commander? Or just enjoying a casual stroll?
"Let's say a bit of both. What were you two talking about just earlier?"
She was asking me for a favor, essentially. She wanted me to investigate something.
While I don't exactly have to keep it secret from you, I'd rather wait until I have all the facts before telling you about it.
"Does it have something to do with Naval HQ?"
Maybe. We'll see. Anyway, let's talk about the operation.
It's strange how the Siren stronghold appearing made Naval HQ do a strategic 180. Don't you think so too?
"It is strange. We need to settle on a course of action as soon as possible, but instead, they're thinking about changing the plan entirely at this stage."
Mhm. They make some... unusual decisions from time to time, but this is on a whole other level.
The operation was going swimmingly, too. We've been winning battle after battle against the Sirens, and even the Ashes.
What's more, it'd be a huge morale boost for everyone if we manage to drive the Sirens out of the NA Ocean. So why stop now?
"The Ashes add an element of uncertainty, but they aren't as immediately threatening as the Sirens are. I'd wager Naval HQ thinks they're a low-priority target."
There's a world of difference between our estimates of their strength and their actual capabilities, too.
Considering Naval HQ aren't the ones fighting on the frontlines, our series of victories must seem inconsequential to them.
And because they're in that mindset, they seem to suddenly think the best option would be to refocus our efforts towards research instead.
It's like the first half of the operation went TOO well, causing Naval HQ's priorities to drastically shift from one extreme to the other.
"I doubt anybody saw this sudden reversal coming."
And I doubt anybody's happy with it either. We still have to investigate the stronghold and all, but...
We shipgirls just want nothing more than to take back the seas from the Sirens.
Naval HQ knows that, and yet here we are.
Ultimately, humanity and shipgirls have the same goal in mind, and it's a simple difference in opinion that's dividing us now...
"Sheffield told me to put the whole thing aside for now. Do you think Elizabeth knows about the situation and plans to use her influence to sway Naval HQ?"
Well, as a matter of fact...
You are entirely correct.
Her Majesty has been informed of your conundrum and is taking an active part in the operation.
And indeed, she is going to work together with other faction leaders to attempt to persuade Naval HQ.
Gosh, don't sneak up on us like that... Didn't you say you were leaving?
Yes, though I still have matters to tend to, so I will be in the area.
I swear, sometimes you act like you're part of the secret service or something...
Please. I am a maid, not a spy.
"Speaking of Elizabeth, I haven't seen her recently. Is she well?"
Her Majesty has been preoccupied with other business as of late, but yes, she is doing quite well. I shall ask her to contact you at a later point.
As I am but a simple maid, I know not what Her Majesty plans to do. But, if you'll allow me to conjecture...
I believe she will arrange an alliance with all the other fleet leaders to put pressure on Naval HQ. Perhaps that will suffice to make them reconsider their decision.
Of course, if such a plan were to come to light, it would considerably impact the Royal Navy's image.
"True. Let's hope that doesn't happen."
Indeed. To that end, I ask you to cooperate with us and play along, Master.
Eagle Union Outpost - The following day
Siren attacks have been getting more frequent with each passing day ever since they established their Core Sector stronghold.
I don't know the purpose behind these attacks. Maybe they're trying to nip our planned offense in the bud, or they're simply gauging our strength.
Whatever the case, our supply lines will be stretched too thin if we don't take the fight to them soon. Then we'll be the ones at a disadvantage.
That's why, today, I'm going to take a stand and try to persuade Naval HQ.
*knock knock*
"Come in."
Hey, Commander. Hope I'm not disturbing you.
"Hey there, Enterprise. What is it?"
Just here to inform you that I've created a fleet to prod the Sirens and gain intel on the size of their force in the Core Sector.
"Well done. Intel on the Sirens is precisely what we'll need to convince Naval HQ."
Yeah. We'll also need to know where they're positioned before we can go on the offensive. Two birds with one stone.
I'll be able to draft an updated mission plan based on the intel as well. Even if the Sirens are more numerous than we expect, I can always request backup or arrange for an evacuation.
All there is to do now is pray Elizabeth is successful on her end.
"I hope so. I heard her discussion about cooperation with the Crimson Axis is dragging on."
...I wonder if Naval HQ will actually let us go on the offensive, even supposing we gain a good picture of the Sirens' strength.
"I'll do everything I can to try to coax them, but I can't make any promises, considering how stubborn they can be."
We're going to lose our advantage at this rate. I think we should try our luck with a daring decision, rather than being caught up in endless hours of debates.
Besides, all things concerning shipgirls at the frontlines fall under your jurisdiction. You are the Commander here, after all.
"You're right... I don't need anyone's approval for this. Let's save the world first, and beg for forgiveness later–– Have the fleet prepare to sortie."
I knew we could count on you. All right, I'll see you down at the port.
It seems the solution to our stalemate was staring me in the face all along...
NA Ocean - Core Sector
It feels like someone has been watching me ever since we set off...
*staaaaaare*
Whuah! Wh-what is it, Commander?
Oh geesh, you noticed I'm feeling nervous, huh...
It'd be hard NOT to notice when someone is staring at you nonstop.
Yeah. You could've stared a hole through the glass with that intense gaze.
Th-that bad? Sorry 'bout that...
It's just... I'm insanely fired up to finally get to fight side-by-side with the Commander! I've been waiting for this day for ages!

options.content: "I've been waiting for a long time for this too."

scripts.say: It's great she's so enthusiastic, but I'm not sure how to respond to that...
Yeah, and why wouldn't I be? You want to save the world, just like a superhero would!
And if you're a superhero, that makes me your sidekick, sort of! Hehehe~
Heck yeah! Together, we'll beat those Sirens and save the world!
You'll be the superhero the world needs, and I'll be your trusty sidekick! Hehehe~
Seriously?! Oh my god, this is the best day of my life!
I'm so happy to hear that, because you're like a superhero in my eyes, Commander! I'm gonna support you 110% in this upcoming battle!
And... if you're a superhero... then that makes me your sidekick, sort of! Hehehe~
Analysis program synchronization complete. We will soon enter the mission zone.
It's getting easier to see through the clouds as we come closer. Looking at it now up-close, it's frightening just how huge this storm is.
Yeah. The storm we observed in the Bermuda Triangle doesn't even hold a candle to this one.
The color and scale being different is one thing, it's the intensity that puts it on another level. Makes me wonder... what if it's a Singularity?
Doubtful. It doesn't really FEEL like the other Singularities we've encountered...
But on the other hand, we know very little about Singularities. If this is one, that could explain why the Ashes keep showing up in these waters.
At any rate, we have to eliminate all the Sirens in the area, and then–
Shoot, they're coming for us! Everyone, get ready to fight!
Detecting approaching Sirens. Preparing for combat is recommended.
(She sensed they were coming even before TB did! That's the kind of intuition that takes a thousand battles to develop!)
There's a good chance they're controlled from a remote command center, judging by how quickly they reacted to us.
"Remember, we're only here to gauge the size of their forces. Don't overextend, and avoid combat if possible."
You heard the Commander. I'll adjust our course to keep us some distance from the eye of the storm. Only engage the Sirens if you need to!
Message incoming from the forward base.
Commander, we've picked up readings that suggest there are Ashes in your area. Keep your eyes peeled and be on your guard.
"Another party throwing their hats into the ring, huh..."
"While I have you on the line... Have you heard anything from Naval HQ yet?"
Nope, not a word so far. I'd take their silence to mean tacit permission to keep doing what you're doing.
Orders received. Downloading Ashes coordinates.
Analysis complete. Based on the signal characteristics, the Ashes member appears to be Hiryuu META. Displaying location on the screen.
Thank god we've managed to decrypt their signals and can actually fight back against them.
Agreed, though it's a shame we can't pinpoint their exact location yet. It doesn't help the bulky decryption machine is extremely tough to transport.
Maybe those scientists back at base can make it smaller somehow...
Yeah. If they could shrink it to fit inside your pocket, we could catch the Ashes out in the open and force them to confront us.
Wait. Something is off here... The only time Ashes emit signals is when they're in combat in a general area.
In other words, if they're trying to stay hidden, they'd want to avoid combat as much as they can.
So then why would she start a fight and reveal her location, especially so close to us? It doesn't make sense...
Seems like she's challenging us to a duel.
Alternatively, she doesn't even know we're here. Whatever the case, how do we proceed?
She's broadcasting her location to us. Even if we ignore her now, there's a good chance she'll just be back later.
I say we accept her invitation and find out what she's after while we still know where she is.
"I agree with Enterprise, but let me also repeat what I said earlier: avoid combat if at all possible. Strive to exchange only words with her, not shells."
"But, just to be sure... TB, send a request for aerial support. Have planes circling in the sky above, ready to attack at a moment's notice."
Orders received. Sending the message to forward base.
"All right. We'll set off once everyone's ready."
There are Siren wrecks everywhere... This must be a whole fleet's worth.
That saves us the trouble of having to do it, I guess?
...You found me. That proves you're able to track me somehow.
So you were saying "come find me" after all. Now, why are you here?
Why are YOU here? I'm sick and tired of being stalked all the time.
It's not too late to surrender, you know. We can work it on amicable terms.
Hah! Surrender to a band of fools allied with Antiochus? Not a chance in hell.
Allied with Antiochus...?
Have you ever even stopped to think about how they developed that coordinate tracker?
Same with that thing you call "TB." Do you have any idea where that technology comes from?
What are you getting at? TB was created by Azur Lane scientists under instructions from Naval HQ.
The same goes for the coordinate tracker. It's a product of human ingenuity, and we have people who've verified that.
Sure, their development could have involved reverse-engineering other technologies, but that doesn't change the fact.
"Reverse-engineering" you call it...
It's rich that you say you've "verified it." Have you seen the things you've supposedly "reverse-engineered?"
I... Not personally, no.
Didn't think so. Then there's no point confusing you further with an explanation. All I'll say is this– I'm tired of being followed around.
Enough talk. Let's finish it here, once and for all.
You want us to fight you? No holds barred?
You heard me right. You, the products of "your world's" ingenuity, and me.
Come at me all at once if you so wish. You already know you don't stand a shadow of a chance against me one-on-one.
Commander... Your orders?
We came here to talk, not to fight.
Moreover, we are guaranteed to suffer casualties if we engage her in all-out combat with such a small fleet...
"There's no need for this to get ugly. We just want to know what you've come here to do."
Rather than let your emotions sway you, you made the sound decision not to fight... You are a wise tactician.
What wasn't wise, however, was trying to initiate conversation with someone from the Ashes in the first place.
It could've cost all of you your lives, had it been Takao you pursued. Consider yourselves fortunate that you found me instead.
Having that said, I did come here looking for a fight, and I don't plan on leaving without one.
I won't kill you, but I will make it so you need to be towed back home. You won't be pursuing me any further.
Oh, and if you're still standing by the end of it all, then I'll tell you something you're going to like. Purely out of respect for your dedication.
Or you could still refuse to fight, and I'll send you to a watery grave.
It sounds like she's telling us to prove ourselves worthy. The stick and carrot, except the stick is death and the carrot is a vicious beating.
She's set on fighting us, that much is certain. Words won't get us out of this, only a show of our strength will.
While our fleet is geared for gathering intel, not for fighting the Ashes, we still do have the support I requested from TB.
Well? What's it going to be, Commander?
"TB, call in the airstrike support immediately. Everyone else, focus on surviving Hiryuu's assault!"
Airstrike support? So you did come prepared. Heh, now this will be interesting!
Ah, you remind me of somebody I knew once... Now I understand why Enterprise is so fond of you.
Come! Show me what you're worth!
She's staying just barely out of range of our cannons... While she's not charging at us, she's not letting up her assault either.
Didn't she say she wanted to finish this? It feels like she's still only testing us.
Wait... Is she trying to drive us off course with her attacks...? Commander, we're slowly drifting towards the center of the NA Ocean!
Hey, you're right! What in the world is she thinking?!
Doesn't she know the Sirens are gonna attack her too if she gets too close?!
Is she planning to use the Sirens to get us off her tail? But then why did she reveal her location to us in the first place?
KABOOOOM!
Out of nowhere, a loud thundering crash rang out in the distance.
What?! She's provoking the Sirens with her planes?!
The Sirens' retaliation came immediately. Hundreds upon hundreds of defense turrets emerged from the storm and opened fire on Hiryuu META.
That entire island... is one giant Siren facility?!
This is the heart of the Sirens' territory... It makes sense they have defense to match that.
Now we have an idea of what we're up against. We can't defeat them here if we don't attack with everything we've got.
This proves my hunch. The Sirens excel at using abnormal weather to their advantage.
We would've never found their defenses on our own... I mean, who'd intentionally steer a fleet into a storm in search of Sirens?
They not only defied human common sense, they even made the storm a part of their defenses.
Seems I was right. You came out here to perform recon on the Sirens...
In that case, think of this as my parting gift. Hope it's satisfied you.
...I mean, we did wanna find out the size of their force, but this is NOT what we were hoping for!
(Hm. The sweetness of an old memory relived is waning already...)
(Curses... I thought I had rid myself of those wretched things long ago...)
Commander, what do we do? We can't fight possibly fight the Sirens and Hiryuu at the same time!
You won't have to, because I'm content to leave it here for today. Farewell.
First you challenge us to a fight out of nowhere, then you decide to flee in the middle of it?
Don't get cocky with me. I'm one of the Ashes, not some damn circus clown here to amuse you.
Hiryuu's planes stopped firing at us... Are we really letting her go, just like that?
We have no other choice, Birmingham. We don't know the full extent of what Hiryuu is capable of, but we did learn a little more about her today.
And besides, like Reno said, we can't possibly fight her and the Sirens at the same time.
Speaking of the Sirens, they're coming straight for us!
"And a lot of them, too. I think we've probed enough for one day."
I agree. We have a pretty good idea of the extent of their presence in the area now.
If we inform Naval HQ about this, they'll take this operation a lot more seriously.
I'm confident they'll make the correct decision once they realize the entire operation is at risk if we don't strike with all the power we can muster.
"Exactly. But before we launch an all-out offensive, we should pay a visit to the Royal Navy's forward base."
Hey Commander, Long Island here, in charge of communications for the day. I've got some orders from Naval HQ for you~
Oh, have you already arrived at the Royal Navy's outpost?
Hehehe, what's the Royal Navy's outpost like?
"It's laid out pretty much the same as any other Azur Lane outpost, but I've been told the interior differs a lot... I've heard it's just as you'd expect from the Royal Navy."
I'd wager they decorated it to look like the boss room of a dungeon. A ghost like me would know~
"I'll find out soon enough. More importantly, what about those orders you were talking about?"
Right, we're in the middle of an operation... I uh, totally forgot this channel was strictly for business...
Anyway, I've got some pretty juicy news for you. Naval HQ took a good hard look at the report you sent, and has approved your plans for a general offensive!
"Now we can finally make our move... Some juicy news indeed."
"So, about our schedule for the offensive..."
Just as you were thinking, the Eagle Union is performing some more reconnaissance and will promptly be at action stations!

Thanks to you already having scouted out their general strength, I was able to take a good look at the status of the Sirens' seas and found a better way to monitor them. You can leave things to me until the operation begins!
Until then, you can just take it easy in the Royal Navy's outpost. Enjoy your time off until all hell breaks loose~
Since we were able to determine that the Sirens' forces were stronger than we thought, it would be wise to secure more information via reconnaissance so we can make any changes we need to our plans.
"By the way, if you're in charge of communications... does that mean there are other logistics-oriented girls stationed here too?"
Hehehe, bingo~ You'll be having a touching reunion with Helena and Memphis soon~!
Signing off, Commander. Have a good one~
Phew... That was nerve-wracking...! Oh crap, the comms are still on!
That didn't quite make sense, but... Whatever, let's just get some rest while we can.
*knock knock*
Please pardon my intrusion. It's good to see you again, Master.
Her Majesty's tea party is fast approaching, so if you would please follow me.
Oh right, Elizabeth invited me to a tea party earlier.
We had hoped to invite you to our castle on the Royal Islands, but... as the situation stands, we had to make do the best we could.

This outpost may be quite modest by comparison, but I assure you the experience will be as if the tea party were being held on the Royal Islands. Her Majesty is personally overlooking the preparations.
"...That eye for details is certainly just like her."
Thank you for your understanding. Her Majesty has been looking forward to meeting with you, Master.
Royal Navy Outpost - Banquet Hall
So this is the... tea party. Feels more like a banquet, honestly.
Not only are there high-quality teas and decadent pastries, but all of the furniture from the Royal Castle's banquet hall is here...
Elizabeth is abusing her position again! Look at all of the unnecessary stuff she had shipped over!
Baseless accusations! I did no such thing!
I paid for all of these furnishings straight from my pocket—Ahem, the royal family's budget! And I must say, your evident jealousy has already made it quite worth it.
Hmph! You're taking advantage of the fact that I'm holding back!
Miss Saratoga, please have some tea to help you relax. Everyone, please help yourselves to the refreshments.
Indeed. You are all free to savour all we can offer!
Well, whether it's a tea party or banquet, as long as it helps boost our morale~♪
I really won't hold back, you know! ...Edinburgh! Get me one apricot cookie, one of each sandwich, and one black tea for the Commander!
Oh, sure! Just one moment, please!
It looks like Saratoga ordered a black tea for me... Well, I suppose why not.
It's pretty good... Aren't you going to try anything, Enterprise? Come on, loosen up! The Royal Navy's snacks are delicious.
Miss Enterprise, may I interest you in a fluffy cranberry scone?
Thank you. Let's see...
The tea party surpassed everyone's expectations. Later, just as it was drawing to a close...
"I've heard Memphis and Saratoga are here to support the operation. They'll be a great help."
Some reinforcements arrived on our side, so we came here to help you guys out~♪
"As we had planned, we'll be joining forces with the Royal Navy, and the offensive will start once reinforcements have arrived."
Geez, Commander! You always go straight into work mode! I was planning on explaining everything to you after the tea party ended...
Previously, you had sent someone proficient in communications to the Royal Outpost to ensure the plan would go smoothly, right?
Naval HQ ended up sending more personnel and supplies than we expected, so we decided to spread our forces out to cover more ground.
"Well, I had given some orders regarding that, but there was no way to know who would be coming over here..."
Not a problem. We won't refuse any able-bodied additions to our ranks!
That's not to imply the operation won't proceed flawlessly with me at the helm, but even one such as I may occasionally need to watch from the sideline.
Sheffy told me everything. Thanks to your efforts, Naval HQ has finally gotten off of their arses.
We must ensure that this offensive is a success. Do not let me down!
"You deserve credit too, you know. Naval HQ definitely wouldn't have responded so quickly if it wasn't for you."
Hoho! Continue to show your gratitude!
With that taken care of, we'll be leaving the rest in our capable Commander's hands. Please behave and go back to your castle, Miss Elizabeth~
Hogwash! I'm already here, am I not? I shall accompany you to the heart of the NA Ocean.
Huh? You're going to head into the center of the NA Ocean... personally?
That is the plan.
That is the only way I can figure out what's happening. I-it's certainly not because I'm worried about my servant here!
Hm~ But Elizabeth, there's no need for you to fight on the front lines, is there...
Just stay where it's safe, and leave the fighting to the Royal Maids. This mission is especially dangerous, and we don't wanna risk you or the Commander getting hurt.
...We understand that, but...
It's fine, Warspite. I know how you feel, but we need not explain ourselves to this close-minded commoner.
And now you're pulling the queen card on me?
This is not up for debate! It would besmirch my reputation to send my servant into danger without incurring any risk myself!
What are you—! Gosh, I'm just trying to show some concern for you!
Save it for someone who needs it!
Well... It seems Her Majesty will be coming along with us.
After the tea party, I was heading for the break room when I ran into Sheffield.
Oh... What a pleasure it is to see you again, Master.
"I couldn't find you at the tea party, but I guess you're here as well."
It's the duty of the Maid Corps to keep this place clean and tidy.
By the way, I have a message for you from Her Majesty.
"You should think about what the existence of the Ashes means for us."
I believe that Her Majesty may have wanted you to mull over this during your mission.
Thank you for your time. Please enjoy your evening.
NA Ocean - Core Sector
The fleet has finished assembling at the designated area. Mission will start in about 10 minutes.
Finally we're moving out again.
Our reconnaissance has confirmed the presence of a tremendous Siren force and a massive stronghold in the center of the NA Ocean.

This operation is massive in scope. Unlike usual, we won't be taking quick skirmishes to knock out their command network. Instead, we'll be pushing our entire forces through for a direct confrontation.
Yep. Considering the size of our respective forces, Naval HQ decided the best strategy was an all-out attack from all directions.
It's very straightforward. All you have to do is steadily clear all the obstacles in your path and eliminate every last Siren you see.
We'll have every fleet from every outpost in the area, all fighting with the same goal in mind. Simple and straightforward, just the kind of strategy I can get behind.
It's not so simple for the girl who has to coordinate the efforts of so many people at once. Anyway...
Our fleet is the biggest one sortieing today, and we'll have the Commander at the helm. I suppose that makes it something of a superfleet.
Especially with Queen Elizabeth herself joining us too~
But, even with the huge fleet we've assembled, we'll still have to break through one defensive barrier at a time to reach the center of the NA Ocean.
Though we have a rough idea of what we're up against, the fact remains that our intel on the whole is limited.
Yup! To summarize, it's not a race, it's a multi-lane Siren-busting marathon to the center!
Bzzzzt––––––––
This is battlecruiser Hood of the Royal Navy fleet. I've been asked to deliver a speech on behalf of the Commander.
Long ago, the Sirens appeared and ushered in an age of terror. Humanity could do nothing but watch as they seized our seas with ruthless aggression.
They were unrelenting and merciless, but despite their best efforts, we refused to yield. Even when we lost battle after battle, we never lost hope of winning the war.
When they would push us to the brink, we would muster all our strength and courage to push them right back. Our resolve was tested, but it never once faltered.
We, as proud members of the Azur Lane, have fought tirelessly to reclaim the seas – to reclaim our freedom and peace. Our battle is far from over yet, but luck is on our side today.
The Sirens in the NA Ocean are in disarray. They are concentrated at the ocean's centre, where a great storm defends what remains of their fleet.
To them, this is their last stand. To us, this is a decisive victory just within reach.
They shall find no stay of execution from us this day. We are the ones who shall turn the cogs of destiny!
Shipgirls, once more, muster your strength and courage with me, and we shall defeat the Sirens!
Let us take back what is rightfully ours, and seize true glory with our own hands!
Commander, kindly give us the order to start!
The operation is scheduled to begin now. All fleets are ready to sortie.
Warning: Large Siren defense structure detected ahead. Readings suggest it is a stronghold cannon.
A cannon of that ridiculous size?! Not even a battleship could endure a direct hit from that!
"We have to destroy it before it destroys us. The question is how..."
Simple – fight fire with fire. We need only blast it to bits with our own firepower!
Ready, George?
Yes, Your Highness. We are loaded and ready to fire.
Commander, let us battleships take care of that cannon.
No matter how sturdy the Sirens fancy their defences, our precise volleys shall render them into naught but dust.
Target acquired. King George V's, blow it to kingdom come!
Take aim! FIRE!
Analysis complete. The route through the area ahead is obstructed by a Siren blockade.
It would take too long to break through or find a way around... Our best option is to destroy what's powering it.
"I couldn't agree any more. TB, you know what to do."
Orders issued. All able fleets are to search for the blockade's power source.
A communications request has been received from an allied fleet. Connecting...
Hehe! Need a hand with anything, Commander?
Tem! Err... Le Téméraire! Mind your tone!
Pardon her. This is L'Opiniâtre, Iris Libre magi– Excuse me, I mean Iris Libre destroyer.
Uhh, please pretend you didn't hear that.
Psst. You nearly slipped up bigtime there, Opie.
Shh, I know, Tem, just be quiet...
As I was going to say: I'm honored to be taking part in this operation. Additionally, I have something to report.
Hehe! See, Opie? I told you so!
We're both so excited to be fighting together with you! Oh right, we've got something to report, too.
We just found what appears to be a Siren power source.
All we've got to do is smash it, and that'll get rid of the blockade, right?
"Based on previous experience up to this point, yes."
Gotcha! The Iris Libre fleet is on the case!
Commander, we have successfully eliminated all Sirens in the area.
Their aircraft proved a tad troublesome to bring down, but they never stood a chance against our combined air force.
Mhm. Once you take out the carriers, their planes lose most of their bite.
Well, we're moving on to the next area then. Good luck over there, or whatever.
Wow! It's amazing what we can do when we really go all-out like this!
It really is. They cleared the entire area, and our fleet didn't even have to fire a single shot.
Hell yeah. Feels like nothing can stop us now.
"Was that Eagle and Perseus just now? I thought they were deployed in the north?"
Surprised? Heheh! I made some arrangements to get them redeployed!
Her Majesty managed to strike an agreement with the Northern Parliament and involve them in the operation as well.
In essence, due to the critical nature of this operation, their participation will not impact the war situation in the north.
When we said we'd send everyone we could, we meant it. Now let us advance and purge this ocean of its Siren blight!
Hey, Commander... Don't these floating fortresses look familiar?
"They remind me of the fortress the Iron Blood is working on..."
Indeed they do. Might I say, researching even ordinary Siren technology is a tall order.
First Mirror Seas, and now floating fortresses...
I can only hope they won't use the fruits of their research against us someday.
Yeah. I don't even wanna think about what would happen if they used Siren tech for evil.
If they decide to switch sides one terrible day... Bleh, it's too scary to imagine...
...We'll have to keep a watchful eye on the Iron Blood. That's for sure.
Warning: Multiple Siren signals have been detected ahead. Their source appears to be a cluster of Tester-types.
Testers, huh? Are they finally sending the real welcoming crew?
They're Tester vessels more specifically, so not quite. Vessels aren't capable of verbal communication.
I've heard reports about them from other fleets. They said the vessels are no pushovers by any means, but apparently they lack a central command unit.
Basically, they're a cut above mass-produced units, though they don't quite rival the elites.
They always have some new surprise in store for us...
Seeing as these are watered-down Testers, safe to say they're sending the toughest thing this defensive line has to offer.
Heh, fine by me. I've been aching for something resembling a real fight!
Scan complete. No Siren signals were detected in the area.
Initiating combat data analysis.
Analysis complete. This fleet and three others have broken through the Sirens' defenses. The first line of defense in the NA Ocean has been breached.
Nice, let's keep up the good work.
Very well. Up next should be the second line of defense. Bel, any news on reconnaissance?
Yes, Your Majesty. The first round of reconnaissance has been completed. There are several stray Siren fleets, but there does not seem to be a sizable force holding the line.
Does that mean... they went all out on their first defense and didn't feel like they had to bother afterward?
Maybe they sent all of their available units to defend the exterior...?
(There's no sound strategy behind this... If they have no Plan B, there are no escape routes or reinforcements. Once they're breached, they've lost.)
(There's no way that we caught them completely unaware...)
Even though each fleet has defeated a large number of Sirens, it's still not as many as we were anticipating.
Moreover, our initial analysis suggested that we would encounter more of their forces the closer we got to the heart of the NA Ocean, not the opposite.

The positioning of the Sirens is questionable for sure... Even assuming the Sirens are all at the heart of the NA Ocean, there's still a mismatch in the number of Sirens we scouted and the number of Sirens we've defeated.
Not only that, if all of them are at the heart, they'd be so tightly clustered they'd only get in each other's way.
Plus, there's no need for them to hide their strength after we've come this far... If they really wanted to halt our advance, they could just group up and try whatever they wanted.
"Great points. We ought to keep our eyes peeled for any strange Siren deployments while continuing with our plan..."
Warning: Abnormal weather detected ahead. Maintaining distance from the anomaly is recommended.
A storm within a storm... That's some extreme weather.
Both storms seem to be spinning at the same velocity, making it appear completely still from the inside... Enterprise, Commander, what do you think?
Yeah. There's no mistaking it. That storm is the same Singularity we saw in Bermuda.
I mean, we've seen a lot of extreme weather before when dealing with Sirens. How can you tell it's a Singularity?
I want to point to its size, wind patterns, and our instrument readings... but honestly? It's just my intuition.
I suppose you're right. A storm that completely blocks off the NA Ocean's center is too big to just be a Mirror Sea. It has to be a Singularity.
Extreme weather that's larger in scope than a Mirror Sea... That makes me think...
The shipgirls who created the Bermuda Singularity... The Ashes... Who created the Singularity over here...?
