Gosh, my head is a mess... Like, if the Ashes created this Singularity, why would the Sirens use it as their base...?
Beats me... Hey, are you all right, Memphis? You sound out of breath.
Now that you mention it... are these... black crystals...?
TB, can you analyze the structure of this stuff?
Orders received. Beginning analysis.
Analysis complete. This material shares similarities with the material used to analyze the Ashes' coordinates, though it is structurally slightly different.
My conclusion is that the Ashes have battled here.
Well, then that makes sense. The Ashes and the Sirens must have fought around here.
Lemme guess... This is what you wanted to see for yourself?
That's correct. Everyone could already have guessed this was a Singularity, but I had to see firsthand what it has to do with the Ashes and the Sirens.
Sometimes it's worth to see the frontlines with your own eyes. Take notes, Commander.
I'm pretty sure the Commander gets out more than you do, but hey...
Bel, go and collect a sample for me, and analyse it back home later.
Certainly, Your Majesty.
Warning: High energy readings have been detected at the eye of the storm. Evacuate immediately.
Hah?! Wh-what? The Singularity is growing all of a sudden...!
Bel! Commander! Flee at once!
The weather anomaly is expanding at a rate exceeding our speed. It is recommended to brace for impact.
Yeah, we can see that! Commander, get over here!
"Wait... The storm isn't expanding into us, it's dragging us inside it!"
There's no escaping its pull...! Hang on to whatever you can!
Do you recognize me?
You're... Enterprise?! But that's impossible... Guh! I thought you already—
Sounds like your cognitive bypass is fine. How'd the battle go? Tell me quick.
Gah... How do you think it went? It's dead quiet here after they... After they decimated us.
The Sirens are pruning the branches, huh.
...Do you want revenge?
Of course I do... They broke me into a thousand pieces...
But... there's no hope left...
Even if I had the power to take down as many as I could... what good would it do...
Those bastards just keep coming... they've wiped out every last one of us, save for me...
You still don't understand your true power, do you?
Even if a flame is extinguished, its Ashes yet remain.
I am Enterprise, but not the Enterprise you know... Ark Royal, will you join us?
Master, are you awake? How are you feeling?
My head is spinning, but I'm able to rise to my feet.
By the looks of it, it seems that the rest of the fleet was drawn into the Singularity along with us.
"So this is what's inside the Singularity... It looks almost like a battle unfolded here."
Miss Baltimore, Miss Enterprise, and Her Highness told me that in case of an emergency, I should look after you.
No need to worry, those are not the remains of our allies.
We are currently searching for our allies through this wasteland. Please rest for the time being, Master.
"What happened to TB?"
TB... hasn't been responding since we were drawn into the Singularity.
The Sirens may be jamming our signals, but since our electronics are also malfunctioning, we can't be certain that's the case.
"Singularities are always more of a pain to deal with than Mirror Seas..."
Fortunately for us, our close-range communications are still working, so we should still be able to regroup with the rest of our fleet.
I'm currently trying to contact them. I will report back to you when I am able to reach them.
Heeding Belfast's suggestion, I closed my eyes and rested for a bit.
Commander... and Enterprise!
Essex! Was the aerial support fleet swept up by the Singularity too?
Yes, so it seems. The storm drew us inside, and the next thing we knew, we were in this place...
Of course, we came looking for you and the Commander as soon as we were able to!
Thank you. It's a huge weight off our shoulders now that you're here. Since we don't have any information about the inside of the Singularity, we can use all the help we can get.
Commander, you don't look so good... Is it due to the trauma you experienced from the storm?
Hold on for a moment, let me examine you...
"So the Singularity sucked in not just our carriers, but our repair ships and rear support too?"
Well, normally, us support vessels shouldn't be on the front lines, but...

I wanted to move the temporary base forward as a contingency in case of unplanned emergencies, and I wanted to make sure that Enterprise and the others were able to get repairs if they needed them. Hehe.
Oh, by the way, since I was around the carriers, I didn't need to worry about combat at all.
Don't overwork yourself, Vestal.
You're one to talk~
You know as well as I do that I'm not pushing myself as hard as you are~♪
Anyway, Commander. I looked over everyone else earlier and nobody's taken any serious damage. They're all doing just fine~
Especially Enterprise over here. She's in perfect condition for this operation.
And there's no way she'll overdo it when she's by your side~ Which is always a good thing.
The goal is just up ahead. There's no point in retiring from the operation this late into it.
While I may not be very useful in a battle, you can always trust me to repair and resupply our fleet!
"Thank you. Emergency repairs are a lifesaver in this situation."
This place may be where the Sirens' fleet has been all along... We need to proceed with caution from here on out.
How are you feeling?
Disgusted, in a familiar way...
Ah, right. You've never been to a test site that's progressed to this stage before.
You mean to say you're used to this?
We agreed not to ask questions about each other's pasts. Don't forget that.
Sorry. It won't happen again.
Save the chitchat for later. The enemy's coming.
Hate to be blunt, but we stick out like a sore thumb here. It's only a matter of time before the Arbiters come for us.
It doesn't matter. They'll pursue us no matter what branch we escape to.
Remember, our mission is to stall them by any means necessary until the Singularity stabilizes. That is all.
How are you feeling, Master?
Belfast and Vestal gave me first aid. I'm feeling much better now.
Think nothing of it, Master. I simply did what is expected of a maid.
That is wonderful to hear. Miss Vestal truly outdid herself.
Comma– Ahem! Servant! Are you all right? No lingering pain, I presume?
Phew... You've recovered splendidly! Quickly now, see what's happening outside!
I got up on the deck of the mass-produced battleship and looked around. What I saw left my jaw agape in shock.
Wrecks. Countless wrecks, littering the sea's surface all the way into the horizon.
So dense that our fleet has to use the bow of a ship to plow a way forward through the wreckage.
This started around half an hour ago...
It began with just a few broken-off fragments floating in with the waves. Then more appeared, and then even more...
Until eventually it got to the point where we are now, struggling to even move forward because of all the debris.
And to think they're all Siren wrecks... I suppose this explains where they all went.
I've never seen such a gruesome sight before. Calling this the site of a battle doesn't do it justice...
It's more like the site of a one-sided slaughter. No... a dumping ground for their broken husks...
There was no hostility in Enterprise's or Memphis's voices. Everyone was simply in shock at what they were seeing.
Layers upon layers of broken metal piled atop each other. No gunfire, no explosion, no screams. Only destruction.
Metal screeches against metal as our ships slowly push past, like the groaning of a demon in the thralls of its final death. But before long, silence had returned.
If I had to describe this scene with just one word... it would be "graveyard."
I solemnly ordered the fleet to keep advancing in formation, launch additional recon planes, and gather intel on the sector as quickly as possible.
The wrecks in this area are still burning, suggesting these Sirens were taken out fairly recently.
Around half the wrecks in this area have sunk beneath the surface, and we found traces of algae. They must've been floating here for quite some time.
This debris doesn't appear Siren in origin. It appears man-made.
It's all so strange. The wrecks seem to have been floating around for wildly differing times, and there's no apparent explanation for where they came from...
I'm willing to believe they're all from Sirens in the NA Ocean, but that they had THIS many here? That just seems impossible.
Unless... Unless there were far more Sirens concentrated here than we observed...
What's your theory? That the bulk of the Sirens' forces was eliminated inside the Singularity?
Yes, it seems the most plausible to me.
It would explain why their defense was so incompetent – they'd already suffered massive casualties before our all-out offensive even began.
If we suppose that's true, then everything adds up. As for who eliminated them, I would speculate it was the Ashes. Though it could've been someone else.
At any rate, this is where the "real" battle took place – where the Sirens made their last stand.
Looking back at it now, the storm and the lack of a strong Siren presence in the area is essentially what put our all-out offensive into motion.
If what we saw earlier was their last-ditch effort to defend their territory... that means that, by pure luck, we struck while they were at their weakest.
However, there's a hole in your theory. If the Ashes are responsible for the fresh wrecks, then who the hell is responsible for those older ones?
Then there's those wrecks of mass-produced ships which are unmistakably man-made. We may have only found a handful, but that handful is still a large percentage of all the ships we have in the area.
If we'd lost that many ships at some point, we would've known about it by now.
Maybe... The old wrecks are from a battle we fought long ago, and they somehow resurfaced much later...?
Still no. There are more here than have sunk in any battle in the NA Ocean at any point in time.
Just look around you. You can send recon planes in any direction and find no end in sight to all these wrecks...
Even seeing it with your own eyes, it's almost impossible to believe there could be so many sunk ships in one place.
Hehe~ As it so happens, I might know an explanation for that!
Really? Do tell.
The common theory goes that Singularities are dimensionally divergent!
What does "dimensionally divergent" mean, exactly?
If I remember right, it's something like... Singularities don't have fixed space in three dimensions. Rather, they exhibit more complex properties.
Ever heard of the observer effect? It's likely the inside of a Singularity is strongly influenced by what its observers see.
Ah yes, that! I've read about this before.
Hey! At least let me finish explaining before you try to steal my thunder!
Well, now is a good time to mention it was OUR Royal scientists who first proposed that theory.
Oh really? What sets their theory apart from the Eagle Union's version of it?
...Bel, look into this matter for me later.
Pfft...
Hey! Don't scoff at royalty! Go on then, continue with your explanation if you're so eager to share it.
All righty then. When the inside of the Singularity is directly observed, it will continue to expand. That's why it seems like there's no end to it.
So the more we explore, the bigger it grows, and the more mass accumulates inside it. And if it grows too big, it could lead to something disastrous!
The good news is, the Ashes and Sirens seem to be able to come and go as they please! Which means there has to be a way out of the Singularity.

options.content: "I don't think I caught all that..."

scripts.say: But to find it, we'll need to stop observing so much. As counterintuitive as it sounds, we should probably put away our planes and radars and rely only on line of sight!
I knew you'd agree, Commander! Then let's get searching!
That's fair. It's pretty complicated stuff. But don't worry, I'll get us out of here in no time!
Stop for a sec! I see people on the horizon!
Some of them definitely look like Sirens. The rest, though... I think they're Ashes.
We can't use TB's scans to identify them since it would mean observing a greater area, yes?
Unfortunately, yeah. Does anyone here have good long-distance eyesight?
Bel, you're up.
Certainly, Your Highness. Let's see... As far as I am able to tell, there appears to be five silhouettes in the distance.
Three of them match the descriptions of documented elite Sirens. As for the remaining two, I concur with Miss Memphis and conclude that they are Ashes.
Two Ashes members in one place? That's gotta be a first.
They seem to be holding their own against the Sirens, too. It's no wonder, given how frighteningly strong they are.
I believe we have encountered these Sirens before. They are Temperance, Strength, and The Hermit. One of the Ashes is Hiryuu, and the other...
...There's no mistaking it. That must be Ark Royal.
The Ark Royal that approached the Eagle Union fleet, hm?
At last we meet, Ashes...
Oh dear, it's her... Now I remember what a nightmare it was to capture her.
Not to mention we didn't have a coordinate tracker back then. Locating her was like trying to find a needle in a haystack...
Fighting them in a sea of shipwrecks sounds like a bad idea. Commander, I think we should keep a low profile and leave them be.
They don't know we're here yet, so now's a good time to–
Pass by unnoticed? Sorry, but it's too late for that.
You came at just the right time. I knew I could count on you to show up when I needed it.
What's the meaning of this, Hiryuu? I know you've been sneaking off on your own for a while now. Suppose you've made some new friends, huh?
Our hit-and-run tactics work fine for dispatching detached Sirens. When invading a stronghold, however, we could certainly use the backing of a big fleet.
And let's not forget we're up against Arbiters here. I'm not afraid to pull a few strings to gain an advantage over them.
I'm aware, but remember what Takao said about minimising contact with outsiders?
It's a little late for that now. They found me before I found them.
Look, the Commander is our golden ticket out of here. I guarantee you the Arbiters won't be coming after us.
Hmph... Whatever you bloody well say.
A small argument broke out between the Ashes members just as we got here.
Ark Royal conceded the argument with a sigh, then directed her gaze at me.
...So you're the one. The Commander she – "Code G" – is so fond of.
Not in the mood for a conversation, eh.
"And you're Ark Royal... Member of the Ashes."
The very same.
You're... an interesting one, Commander. I've heard the tales about you.
Are you... Are you really Ark Royal?
Your High––
...Yes, I am. Mind you, I may not necessarily be the Ark Royal you know.
...You don't need to know anything more than that.
...Very well.
Please don't take offense, she's always like this. Having said that, perhaps you should take a leaf out of her book.
Getting back on topic... Based on all your actions up to this point, it's safe to say you in fact are not allied with Antiochus.
That being the case, I'd like to propose a temporary truce between us. Together, we can get out of this sticky situation. What do you say?
What do I think? Thinking and making decisions is your job, you doltish servant!
It's your call, Commander. I'm behind you either way.
I can't say whether the Ashes are friends or foes, but if nothing else, they can be reasoned with. Sirens, meanwhile, are the antithesis of everything we stand for.
Things probably aren't quite that clear-cut. Just saying...
If nothing else, this is a good opportunity to gather intel on the Ashes. That's worth something.
We won't stop you from taking notes. After all, we're the ones asking for help here.
You sound sure we won't learn anything useful. We never wanted to fight you, you know. We just wanted to understand you. That's what the Commander wanted all along.
I see... Be that as it may, you aren't as trustworthy as you'd like to think you are. That's all I'll say on the matter.
At any rate, I'm certainly not opposed to occasionally teaming up to defeat a common enemy. Like now.
...An unexpected development has occurred. Should we abort the mission?
Yeah, no. The risk's still well within an acceptable range. Continue as planned.
Agreed. Stick to the mission. Eliminate the invaders so we can reinstate normal test site conditions.
I'll have faith in your assessments, then. Proceed as proposed.
Doesn't look like we have much choice here but to join forces with the Ashes...
"All ships! Target the Arbiters! Open fire!"
Do NOT let them get in formation! Keep taking them out until the Enforcers go into hiding!
Got it! Leave the small buggers to me!
Not bad, but it ends here. My web was already spun before you launched your first attack. Execute combat link protocol.
On it! Executing IX-XIV Linked Jamming Protocol!
For some reason, weapons output 7.3% less damage than expected. A curious phenomenon.
They're bloody jamming my weapons systems, Hiryuu! You'll have to take over for me for a while!
Son of a... Always coming up with dirty new tricks to use on us...
The Arbiters are focusing their jamming on the Ashes. They're open to attacks from us.
The battleship fleet is locked and loaded!
Our plane squadrons are ready for takeoff too! We'll hit 'em right where it hurts!
(Ah, it's been ages since I was part of a large joint operation... I'm ablaze with motivation!)
The Ashes are something else! Just one of them is enough to match the firepower of several of us...
I'm just glad we were somehow able to make up for the reduction of Ark Royal's power.
(Actually, I feel like we did more than just make up for it. I've heard the Ashes differ in how strong they each are, but I guess the gap between them and us isn't as big as we thought.)
(This is crucial information for us. I'll have to add it in my report to the Commander later.)
It's pretty troubling that we don't have a grasp on the true strength of the Arbiters. Stay focused.
One thing's for sure though – they're strong enough to keep the Ashes on the back foot. The moment we underestimate them may be our undoing!
Look at that, the test subject fleet possesses firepower exceeding our estimates. This is some interesting data.
Did we not just calibrate the parameters of our test vessels?
Seems there's a discrepancy between our simulated and actual performance. Saving the data log for later.
Anyway... Strength, go ahead and crank up the gravity fluctuations.
On it.
Executing IX-XIV Linked Jamming Protocol.
We're in trouble... If all three of the Arbiters team up, this situation is going to get exponentially harder to deal with!
You've got some determination, Commander.
"I've been through my fair share of battles. The more precarious the situation, the more essential maintaining your composure is. Only by staying calm can you even begin to hope for victory."
"Go and take the injured to the rear, and have our repair ships look after them! Press on!"
Leave the injured to me~ No need to worry, we're here to back you up!
The Royal Navy refuses to fall. We will persevere!
Exactly as you say. Please find a safe place at the back of our ranks, Your Majesty.
Enterprise, your flight deck! Go get some emergency treatment, and leave this to us!
All right, will do. Hang in there!
"Ashes, you've taken serious damage. Our repair ships could fix–"
Thanks, but we'll have to pass. You haven't even seen our true power yet.
In case you weren't aware, the Arbiters will annihilate you lot the moment we relax our assault.
She's right. Worry about yourselves before you even begin to think about us.
Having said that, it might be a good idea to take you up on that offer. Let's step back for just for a while to resupply.
Hiryuu……？
No need to get worked up. Have you fought alone for so long that you've forgotten the other tactics available to you as an entire fleet?
"Precisely. Work together with us as allies, or none of us are leaving this place...!"
Temperance, put some pressure on their rear units. Strength, swap over to linked mode, now. We can't let the Ashes recover.
Got it. Switching Linked Jamming Protocol code from IX-VIII to VIII-IX, prioritizing mobility.
Initiating VIII-XIV Linked Jamming Protocol. Let's see their rear guard try to heal off the damage now.
"How's Vestal and the escort fleet looking?"
Thanks to the immediate reaction from the Ashes, they seem to have barely scraped by.
The rest of us are in trouble, though... The Ashes can't attack while resupplying, so all the attacks they were drawing get redirected to us instead!
They've got insane defense, insane offense, and even gravity wells... Even with the Ashes' help, if this draws out, we're toast!
"We need to find a way to break through, and fast..."
I'll strike them from underneath. Their attacks don't work on submarines.
Huh? An Iron Blood submarine?
Mhm. VIIB-class submarine, U-47, at your service.
How did you get in here?
Same as you. I and my team got sucked into the Singularity while scouting ahead for Iron Blood's side of the all-out offensive.
And so I'm joining forces, at the Commander's request.
So the Crimson Axis... were fighting Sirens with us all along!
All right, Commander! Let's try striking at them with the help of our Iron Blood friends here!
Whether one sides with the Azur Lane or the Crimson Axis is unimportant to this operation. This isn't about us versus them, it's about humanity versus the Sirens.
All right, I'm heading off then.
Ready to fire full torpedo load. Say goodnight, Arbiters...
A formidable blow, but ultimately futile. Initiating automatic repair functions.
She's rapidly repairing all the damage the submarines inflicted to her!
And it's not just Strength... The other Arbiters are also repairing themselves!
Does that mean... all Arbiters come equipped with self-regenerating systems?
This vessel's self-repair mechanisms seem to be deficient.
...But no matter. We continue the attack.
"We're only going to be whittled down if this goes on, just as Saratoga said."
"If only there was a way to retreat..."
If you want to retreat, then go right ahead. But we have no intention of running with our tails between our legs.
Our goals are twofold. To defend the Singularity that our allies opened, to the bitter end; and to destroy all of our enemies in one fell swoop. Retreat isn't an option.
So it really was you that created the Singularity all along.
You only figured it out just now?
We can speculate all we want, but we couldn't know for sure until we heard it straight from your mouth.
(So the things that happened to the NA Ocean aren't their fault... And if anything, it was this Singularity that allowed us to finally make a decisive move against the Sirens.)
What's the purpose of you doing all this?
It doesn't concern you... or so I'd like to say.
But that wouldn't be entirely accurate.
Hiryuu！
Yes, I know. I have no intention of saying any more than that.
Let's get down to the nitty-gritty, Commander.
The Arbiters are only after us. There's no reason for you to risk your lives defending this Singularity either.
If you want to retreat like you wanted to earlier, we won't stop you. I'll even tell you the way out.
I swear on the 2nd CarDiv's honor that we won't turn on you. Now tell me, honestly, would you rather stay and fight, or retreat to safety?

options.content: "...No. I won't turn my back on you."

scripts.say: <color=#ff5c5c>Warning: This choice will impact the story. Are you sure about this? You will be able to pick a different choice later.</color>
I see. The well-being of your allies is paramount, so the choice is obvious.
Well, then this is farewell. I'll be hoping for your safe escape.
"As soon as I get in touch with Naval HQ, I'll ask for some reinforcements."
While I don't doubt that you would do that for us, don't bother.
It'll just end up being a hindrance to us. Now go, get out of here, quick.
"All ships! Disengage from the Arbiters, retreat, and change course for the Singularity's exit!"
I wish you the best, Commander.
And that takes care of that. Are you starting to understand how Takao felt, Ark Royal?
The Commander truly is a unique person. A person who's caring and considerate to allies, yet ruthless to enemies. A person who can win anyone over...
A person who accurately reads the flow of battle and is quick to make judgments, and depending on the situation, prioritizes the best interests of the fleet...
Knowing all that, I understand why the Commander made that choice.
Look at it from the Commander's perspective. We're neither friends, nor foes... Just strangers to steer clear of, lest we turn on you.
If I were in the Commander's shoes, I would've likely made the same decision.
Admittedly, as would I, and without hesitation either.
Hiryuu... Thank you for letting me be part of a brief, but blissful dream.
You're welcome. Though I have to admit, I was only half-committed to making all this happen.
No, you absolutely went through a lot of trouble to lead the Commander to us. It was very roundabout, and not something I'd expect from you.
Hahaha, you're not wrong... My sister isn't here, so I guess I ended up doing something that's not in my nature.
Do you think... after the brief time we spent with the Commander, the long-extinguished flames in our heart can be lit once more?
Perhaps... but that no longer has anything to do with us.
Ark Royal, get ready to push yourself beyond the limit. We need to hold out until Enterprise comes back.
...Yeah. I'm aware.
Antiochus... I've long waited for this opportunity... The opportunity to finally have my revenge!
Whatever your goals once were, and whatever you strive to achieve in the end, it's all meaningless to me!
All that matters is that you took away everything I held dear! You destroyed all hope I had!
Humanity has an age-old adage... An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth...
TAKE THIS! ALL OF MY RAGE, FOCUSED IN ONE HIT!
My eyes were stabbed by the blinding light of an explosion. The shockwave tore at my skin, and the blast sent great ripples across the sea.
After the smoke cloud dissipated and the dust settled, there was only deathly silence.
*cough cough*... Commander... you alright?
"I think I'm fine. I'm more worried about everyone else..."
That blast definitely did us no favors. It was like salt in our still open wounds...
Thankfully, the damage to our repair ships and rear fleets was minimal. Our wounded received emergency repairs, so at least there were no casualties.
Plus, the explosion helped destroy a lot of the obstacles that were in the way earlier, so it should make getting out that much easier.
"An explosion of that magnitude... There's no way even the Ashes could have made it out unscathed..."
I understand how you feel, but we're in no position to go back for them.
There's nothing to suggest the Arbiters are chasing us, but we're not out of the woods yet.
"We can't waste the chance the Ashes graciously created for us..."
"We need to escape the Singularity and meet up with our allies on the outside."
"After that, we'll regroup, return to the Singularity, and hopefully return the NA Ocean to the way it was before... A clear, blue sea."
"Until then, just try to hang in there, everyone!"
So, you'll fight with us?
"We may not be in a formal alliance, but we're still allies in the fight against the Sirens. We're not leaving you to fend for yourselves."
Cut it out. We're not your allies.
...But, we are grateful for your help.
You're fine with this arrangement, right? Ark Royal?
...You really are a puzzling personality, Commander.
The Sirens are heartless creatures, basing their decisions entirely on what benefits they stand to gain. I suppose you are the opposite of that.

"As we've established, we're all in this together. Despite our combined efforts, though, we're still slowly getting worn down. I'm sure you both already know we are going to lose if this battle drags on."
In other words, we need reinforcements.
"Can you request assistance from the other Ashes? Like Enterprise, or Takao?"
I wouldn't hold my breath. Nobody knows when they'll come back.
However, there are still other options available to us.
Ark Royal, go with the Commander, and call for reinforcements! I'm going to boost my output up to the very limits!
What?! Are you bloody mental, Hiryuu?!
Did you just notice?
(I've got no choice but to pray that Enterprise's judgment was correct...)
––––Antiochus! See how you like THIS!
I've finished running the combat simulation. We're almost at our limit.
Indeed... Our energy usage has reached the maximum threshold. We cannot maintain this for much longer.
Pull back, Strength. We cannot win once the Ashes launch their counterattack.
I'm detecting a surge in energy. Simulating intended purpose––
They're probably planning to take us all out, including themselves, in a huge explosion.
Restarting damage simulation... It shouldn't matter.
An explosion of the projected magnitude within the Singularity will cause damage to our vessels... but will also prove lethal to the Ashes.
We, however, can survive and reconstitute.
Yeah, but then we'll lose our test subjects.
That is true. They would be atomized in approximately one-thousandth of a second.
Zero gave us instructions to minimize contact with the test subjects.
And? What's your point?
Her point is: the explosion would cause excessive damage to the test site and subjects, making it impossible to complete our initial objective.
My proposal is to allow the test subjects to live. Override your elimination directives.
......Acknowledged. Prioritizing Zero's directives. We will pursue the Ashes with new vessels.
Ditto. Carrying out this directive would entail the failure of other, higher priority ones.
Temperance, cover me. I've had enough of being outside.
Very well... Disengaging from hostiles.
I was blinded by a dazzling light. The attack and subsequent shockwaves I braced for, however... They never came.
Instead, it seemed as though the world faded into pure white, all sound vanishing along with it.
When the light cleared, the Arbiters and their Enforcer-class minions were all gone without a trace of their existence.
Did we win...? How...?
Did the Arbiters retreat after feeling threatened by that attack?
That was a close call...
I turned to look at the Ashes, who seemed like they'd exhausted every iota of energy within them.
I'm... fine... We barely managed to stop them...
Don't worry about me, I'm used to this... Give me a few minutes and I'll be as good as new.
You madwoman... I can't believe that worked.
To be honest, I'm just as surprised as you that it did.
(Somehow, I get the feeling that things are starting to look up now...)
Ah, Commander! What happened to U-47?
While Arbiter was distracted, she escaped in order to contact our allies.
That's a relief... We'll be able to see everyone again...
"If everything's gone according to plan, then our allies on the outside should have cleared the Singularity's surroundings of all enemies already."
Then it's time to bid farewell. With the Arbiters gone, we have no reason to stick together.
In order to get out of this Singularity, head to the exit I told you about earlier, and you should be fine.
We, however, still have some loose ends to tie up here.
Before I could even get a word in, Ark Royal activated her camouflage and vanished. Hiryuu, on the other hand, remained in plain sight.
If you're thinking about coming with me, then don't even try. Don't make me threaten you with what I nearly used on the Arbiters a minute ago.
Sorry, let's not end this on a threat. You brought back fond memories I haven't felt in so long.

options.content: "Wait. What about the thing you said before our duel earlier?"

She's got the same stealth camo as Ark Royal?!
W-wait! Don't go!
The operation had its ups and downs, but we've successfully completed stage one of purging the ocean's core of Sirens.
Although the Singularities and Mirror Seas there haven't gone away, the threat posed to the area has decreased drastically.
The NA Ocean has become safer to traverse, and we're reclaiming routes previously occupied by Sirens, one at a time.
All this isn't to say we can let our guards down, however.
Mindless Arbiter vessels and Sirens still emerge from the Singularity from time to time, and the ever-elusive Ashes remain in the back of our minds.
In order to succeed with our long-term plans, we will need more time and a bigger fleet.
Once all the shipgirls that fought in this operation have received their commendations, daily life at port will resume as normal.
And so, our war against the Sirens continues...
Now it is time for us all to rest up in preparation for whatever challenge comes next.
Analyzing data logs...
Analysis complete.
Commencing footage playback.
Today, we will discuss what has been dubbed the "meta phenomenon."
"Meta" itself is derived from an ancient word which means "change."
It is quite broad in meaning, but for our purposes, it refers to the result of a property having undergone change.
The process itself of a property changing is what is known as "metamorphosis."
This process has been observed in Wisdom Cubes. These Wisdom Cubes make up the processing centers of our autonomous naval combat platforms... colloquially known as "shipgirls."
Cases of metamorphosis has been observed in certain shipgirl subjects as well. When their cores undergo metamorphosis, it affects their quantum data on a fundamental level.
Once a subject's Wisdom Cube has undergone metamorphosis, it cannot be reversed. At least, not through any means currently known to us.
The conditions that cause metamorphosis lie dormant in all shipgirls. Furthermore, its onset metamorphosis can be manipulated, to a certain degree.
If metamorphosis is allowed to progress unimpeded, a subject's Wisdom Cubes will ultimately turn into an Origin Cube.
It is theorized that if are able to induce late-stage metamorphosis in a subject, they–
...More electronic interference? How is that possible? We are deep below the–
Error during data log analysis.
Playback interrupted.
You cleaned up the trash. Thanks for doing your part!
You’ve cleaned up all the trash in the vicinity of the port. Mission complete!
You’ve successfully completed the Energy Matrix experiment. Mission complete!
You’ve successfully fought off the Sirens attacking the port. Mission complete!
You’ve successfully fought off the Sirens attacking the port. Mission complete!
You’ve finished the naval exercise. Mission complete!
You’ve finished the naval exercise. Mission complete!

You’ve retrieved the supplies scattered around the zone. Mission complete!
You’ve retrieved the supplies scattered around the zone. Mission complete!
You recovered the supplies. Awesome!

You’ve recovered the supplies scattered around the zone. Mission complete!

You’ve successfully taken out the Sirens. Mission complete!

You’ve eliminated all the Sirens in this zone. Mission complete!
友方的商船被敌军包围了！
System is being jammed. Navigation menu cannot be displayed.
Abnormal heat signatures have been detected in target sector. Using a different route is recommended.
The fleet is about to enter a whirlpool. Movement capabilities will be impaired.
Having discovered the existence of the Veil with her power of examination, Queen Elizabeth META didn't go a step further and use her insight. She went easy on herself, as she had only just recovered.
Following this, she invited Hornet META and her companions to a training site to provide tactical guidance on their combat capabilities.
That is, until the 7th Task Force received an order to sortie from War Protocol Moon.
I have received an emergency alert from the front lines.
A corrosion phenomenon has occurred within the jurisdictional area of Alaska Command, accompanied by a localized spacetime anomaly of unknown origin.
As the fleet stationed there, the 7th Task Force is to head to the site immediately, eliminate the corrosion phenomenon, and determine the cause of the spacetime anomaly.
Hm? Corrosion's shown up? Aw, crap! We've gotta hurry, folks!
Sorry, Elizabeth, we just got tasked with an urgent mission. We'll continue this some other time!
Hang on a sec... There's no rule against other shipgirls coming along with us on a mission, is there?
And, and! Elizabeth should really see the corrosion phenomenon for herself to get a better understanding of our world, am I right?
Yeah, totes! You'll come with us, won't you, Lizzy?!
I wanna see how you fight!
I concur! Bring your train, too!
I'm also interested in seeing your fighting style. Will you come with us?
...Please?
Well, if you lot are going, then we're certainly coming along.
We're equally curious about your combat styles. Plus, this is a good opportunity to learn more about each other.
Dewey, I've finished reconning the area. I'm synchronizing the data now.
Data received. Beginning analysis.
Border of corroded area detected. Area analysis complete.
Weak spot of corroded area detected. Strike routes have been assigned.
Marking high-priority targets. Assigning mission objectives.
This is our order of engagement.
First, we analyze the area, then use drones to incrementally seize control and clean up while the shipgirls directly deal with the priority threats.
This corrosion phenomenon's nothing! It'll be a walk in the park for us to take head-on!
Since our targets have been assigned, I'm gonna lead the charge!
KABOOOM!
The corrosion phenomenon began to rapidly shrink in size under the 7th Task Force's coordinated assault.
Quite impressive. You're making light work of this thing.
...They can only use their floating battleships and unmanned combat groups. They haven't even unlocked the War Protocols' weaponry yet.
It's a husk of a Council Task Force. It doesn't hold a candle to the real deal.
Pardon? Is a true Task Force really that powerful?
More powerful than you, even?
Powerful enough to bring you down, at least.
Hmph. Not a joke we take in good humour.
Why don't we give it a shot? I'll give you a fair assessment.
Well, how about you go first? Then we shall assess the difference in strength between you and these girls.
There won't be anything left for you if you pit me against these small fry.
Then so be it. There will always be another time.
*sigh*... So much talking.
I'll do it.
...What?!
Using an attack method that disrupts spatial stability, Essex forcibly dismantled the existential structure of the corrosion phenomenon.
While the immediate threat vanished in an instant, the group was then thrown into a more pressing crisis.
Essex! We came here to investigate the spacetime anomaly! You can't simply bugger up space like that!
The anomaly is far more dangerous than any bloody corrosion phenomenon!
Is this how the Ashes always do things?!
Um...
...It's fine. I'll stabilize the area somehow.
Enterprise META's rigging seemed to be connected to a vast array of devices within its storage space.
She activated one of these devices, which gradually brought the spatial anomaly in the whole area under control.
Is that... technology from the alpha timeline?
Just standard equipment for a Task Force.
Standard equipment from... much later on.
Do you see the gap in power between us now?
How many relics from the alpha timeline do you have?
I don't like the word "relic."
That said, I've got a few...
...Huh?
Looks like another spacetime anomaly has come up.
It isn't Essex's fault. Some enormous energy entity is approaching from the outside.
Approaching from the outside?
Yes, we can feel it... Something is coming!
In the harsh light, I remembered a few things.
After the conference, Lexington made a rare homecoming from the front lines.
I heard the final tally.
612 in favor, 219 against, 169 abstentions. The proposal was sent to the Standing Committee for a vote.
The committee voted 11 in favor, 11 against, and no abstentions... No majority vote.
In the end, they invoked the impasse resolution system, and the Antiochus system voted in favor of a counterattack.
...Their decision has been made. All we can do is, do our best.
Besides, we aren't guaranteed to lose. It's just that every single step we take has to be perfect.
I promise, we will win.
Okay. I have faith in you, Commander!
Thus began the decisive battle that I was powerless to prevent.
I experienced the joys of small victories, the anxiety of every stalemate, the horror of every drop of bad news...
And... the pain of seeing Lexington self-destruct with my own two eyes because we were mere seconds too late.
She always put off her Type-II retrofitting, letting other shipgirls take advantage of those resources.
She took my advice and refused to resort to METAmorphosis.
In the end... she protected Saratoga, Helena, and everybody else in the fleet.
So I swore that, as long as the Wisdom Cube network remains intact, I'll do whatever it takes, pay whatever it costs, to see her resurrected.
Unbearable pain shot through me.
It is unbearable, isn't it?
Helena... We meet again.
Long time no see, Commander.
She approaches me, still bearing that same mysterious smile.
After leaving you, I interfered with the Antiochus' transboundary experiment in test site theta and seized their research results.
The Veil of Immunity – technology that can truly protect the world from the X.
The world you see now was born from this technology.
I sculpted this future. The perfect future that everyone deserved.
Then, I separated this branch and all of its possibilities from the collective – like taking a cutting from a plant.
Freeing it from the influence of test site alpha, allowing it to grow anew in a land far divorced from the past.
We walk side by side on the vast, white beach.
Were you happy, Commander?
Hmm... Half yes, half no.
That world is beautiful, but it doesn't have you. How could anyone call it perfect?
But it has everybody else.
Myself versus the rest of the world... I think it's an easy decision, don't you?
Don't be greedy and say you want both.
A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush, you know.
If "both" isn't an option, then I choose to abstain.
Maybe that world will become reality if I have faith in it...
But I could never.
How long can you sustain this all on your own? Five years? Ten? Fifty?
Whatever the case, this perfect future isn't forever.
Hehe... My original plan did involve it lasting forever.
But you see the result. I did my very best, but in just over ten days, it's been poked full of holes.
I couldn't do it all on my own.
So Commander... Will you help me?
Huh?
She makes a surprising proposition.
You're the basis of hope, the seed of miracles, and the key to cognitive awakening.
You and I could be the gods who protect this perfect future.
That way, you and I, along with all the people of the world...
All of us will make it. You can have everything your heart desires.
What do you say? Is this an acceptable offer?
Do you accept, or do you refuse?
Sometimes, Commander, we have to make a decision.

sequence: "Now is the time to choose."

options.content: (On second thought, I don't know about this...)

scripts.say: <color=#ff5c5c>Warning: This is an important choice that will affect the ending. Are you sure?</color>

options.content: (On second thought, maybe it's not such a bad idea after all...)

scripts.say: <color=#ff5c5c>Warning: This is an important choice that will affect the ending. Are you sure?</color>
I accepted Helena's proposal.
She stopped for a moment, but instantly after, she dove into my arms.
The two of us became one in a flash of light.

sequence: On the eighth day after our arrival in Anchorage, the solar wind gradually subsided. In turn, the geomagnetic storm and aurora faded.
The Council investigation turned up fruitless.
After all, every anomaly had been fixed.
The effects of the Mass Syncopes disappeared over time, and so too did the memories of their dreams.
A few days later, the world was peaceful.
Everyone had forgotten about that little affair.
Lexington, Enterprise, Memphis, Anzeel, Sophia, and everyone else who'd gone on that painful journey...
They lived in a perfect new world.
They lived happy lives.
I sent Helena to test site beta.
Thanks to the conceptual flaws within test site beta, we managed to revive Lexington through the same means we used for Amagi.
After that, we covered test site beta in the Veil of Immunity.
There are dimensions to times, too.
To this day, I continue to be the Commander of test site beta.
In the new world, the concept of Helena had disappeared.
But I still remembered her.
After all, she was right in front of me.
I could see her. I could touch her.
We built a home on a new platform, which we called the Helena Layer.
In that new home, we continued exploring the mysteries of the Wisdom Cube network.
We never stopped searching for the answers of higher dimensions.
Even infinity has its gaps.
Maybe we'd never be able to unravel the secret of the X.
Maybe we'd never be able to leave the protection of the veil.
But under this veil...
We had freedom.
"A new world, a perfect world."
"For one story..."
"To finally come to its happy ending..."
"That's more than enviable enough."
"Don't you think?"

scripts.say: ...I'm sorry, Helena. I can't accept that offer.
She gazed at me, displaying neither joy nor sorrow, leaving me no option but to speak.
There might be some special quality to me.
But how did that quality arise, and how special is it, really?
Am I really enough to help you shoulder the weight of an entire world?
You and I know exactly what pain comes with misusing technology we don't fully understand.
The Council has already made the decision to support my actions.
They support my efforts to restore history to its true form.
So I'm sorry... but I just have to deny your proposal.
*sigh*...
Helena bites her lip and sighs softly.
Your thoughts, Lexington?
Lexington stands on the beach not far from us. Maybe she was there the whole time – I just never noticed her.
Commander, you swore that you'd revive her someday, no matter what it takes.
I made the same promise.
For now, at least, we've kept that promise.
Thank you, Helena... Thank you so much.
I'm so happy that you made it out alive that day.
But...
No matter what happens, I'm always on the Commander's side.
I made my decision long before we came here.
This world might be real, and our souls might be real, too.
But that reality only exists based on your observations.
The future you sculpted was only perfect in your own heart.
You're not a god. You can't bear this burden on your own.
At this rate, you'll die...
...I don't care.
I care! I can't stand the thought, and neither can our Commander!
You said it yourself. It's barely been two weeks, if that, and the world is at its limit.
What good would adding the Commander to the equation do?
You're not omnipotent, and neither is the Commander. The Antiochus system surely isn't, either.
Everybody makes mistakes. What happens when you do? Do you just paint it over with more lies?
What do you do when the world has nothing left but contradictions?
This isn't perfection. Not by a long shot.
Lexington's voice quivers, but she does her best to stay calm.
Helena, do you think Anzeel and all the others WANT to live in a world where you're the god in charge of everything?
I have my doubts.
Helena. If you wanted, you could ignore our opinions and force your plan through.
Nobody would be able to refuse. If you took away all of our memories of the past, you'd have your way.
You didn't, though.
You preserved our memories, giving us the right to choose.
That means you'll support our decision. Won't you?
She gazes at me, eyes red from crying. I face her head-on.
Okay... I'll do as you wish.
Finally, she gives me a gentle smile.
Everyone was happy in the past two weeks. I was happy, too.
That's enough for me...
You were on the right track, Helena.
Our future SHOULD be this perfect.
But the perfect future ahead of us is one that we have to fight for.
Have faith.
If we keep on walking forward with hope and volition in our hearts...
Our story won't have a sad ending.
Yes... I have faith in you, Commander.
I'll always believe in you...
Amidst the azure torrent, the world is enveloped in light.

sequence: "It's time to awaken from this perfect dream."

scripts.say: KABOOOM!
The sea's surface shone like quicksilver as enormous beasts rampaged in it.
Enty, Yorktown, what is that weird thing? Is it another mimic beast?
That is an unformed Class VI. No, it might even be a Class VII.
Hornet, keep an eye on the anti-gravity device. Don't get trapped.
Got it! I won't!
You know... I never thought I'd one day get to fight side by side with you both.
Doesn't matter whether it's a Class VI or a Class VIII – I'm not scared of it as long as you're here!
And I will fight with all I've got!
Yorktown, don't do anything reckless.
Your current state is extremely unstable. You shouldn't be fighting in the first place.
You're mistaken. In this environment, the terms that maintain my existence are quite stable.
I can't just stand by and watch while the rest of you are fighting.
Don't be worried. As long as I don't unleash my full power, it'll be fine.
If anything, you should be the one holding back. Try not to disrupt the space's stability and interfere with Moon's support work.
Of course.
...What?
It's been a while, old friends.
Heh. Didn't we all just meet in that perfect dream?
Well... It was no more than a dream, as you just said.
Am I mistaken, or have the Ashes lost quite a few of their members?
Not exactly. It's more like we're too spread out.
Aye. This is all we could muster on such short notice.
At least that much hasn't changed...
Hahaha! Some things have. We've got a new HQ, for one.
Y'all wanna come and pay us a visit sometime?
A new headquarters? Yes. I'd love to come if I do get the chance.
Ahh... That over there's the local Cleveland. In the sky, we've got Helena.
If she gets down and joins us, the Ace Trio would be back together.
There was an Ace Trio? They must've been the cream of the crop!
Heheh... There's a ton of powerful people gathered here. That's gotta mean the enemy's especially powerful, too.
Bigger targets mean bigger rewards for killing 'em!
I'll bet there're loads of tasty food in that big city. Once the fighting's over, I'm going there to have a feast! Awooo!
Pfft. It must be nice – living in the moment, unbound by the past.
Everyone, pay attention. A vector zone has just appeared.
This time, we shall show them the full might of the Ashes!
To battle!
Um...
Goodness, the mood is heavy here...
Say, Friedrich, have you–
I heard about the near-superimposition event.
Eep!
Ahem... Okay! So you heard!
What about it? It was indubitably I who was responsible for it! I don't deny or hide it!
More importantly, behold this power that I've gained! Impressive, no?!
The air trembled, and the giant, silver-white phantom and the mighty-looking aircraft appeared behind Marco Polo.
It's not bad. And?
"And"?
Although she wasn't sure why, Marco Polo sensed an immensely oppressive aura coming from Friedrich der Große's calm look.
She felt almost like she'd descend into an eternal hell if she made even one mistake.
And... Ahahaha... I'll use it to clear the path for you, of course!
Watch me, Friedrich! I'm not the same person I used to be. I shall obliterate the enemy before it even comes near you.
Ohohoho!
Splendid.
Friedrich, that power of yours...
Don't be surprised. I've merely taken another step further as a blueprint shipgirl.
I must say, though – you've done well, Bismarck.
Yes... We've finally gotten through those dark times.
Now, let us fight side by side! For a better future!
Naturally. Our medley begins now.
Seems quite a few Arbiters have gathered here.
Hey, Hunter, do you see the Arbiter that helped you all those years ago?
I'm not sure. Maybe she isn't. Or maybe my memories of her were completely erased.
Whatever the case, I don't sense anyone familiar here.
If none of them feel familiar, then it's safe to say she isn't here.
Ah... Well, that's still something. It means you can count out everyone who IS here.
...More extradimensionals are coming.
Those terrifying beasts cannot be allowed to ravage this beautiful world.
We must stop at nothing to protect it...
Comrade Soyuz begged me to go, which is why I came to help.
Standing here now, I realize... This is an exceptional place.
With exceptional people, exceptional things...
I am stunned by how vast the world is.
Now might be the time to take another step forward...
BEEP BEEP!
Your Majesty, I have encountered enemies in combat sector 26. Beginning engagement.
Alright. The Queen's Light is standing by to provide support. You may fight with confidence.
Understood.
Ah, one more thing. Everyone, listen closely.
This is not a localised battle of annihilation, it is an all-out defensive war.
Pay close attention to your adjacent sectors, coordinate extensively with your nearby allies, and always be ready to work together to eliminate the enemy!
Heh... An enemy has appeared even before us now.
Get into positions! Take it down!
We meet again, Memphis.
Have you remembered anything? Your expression says so.
Long time no see, Hiryuu.
Yeah, I guess you could say I have. I used to get Helena to seal off some of my memories to stabilize my resculpting phase.
Things have changed now, though. I'm sure it's fine to release some memories.
Oh. So that's what it was. All this time, I thought... No, never mind.
You said, "things have changed." I assume that has something to do with what happened inside the Veil – correct?
As in... the dream that only we experienced.
Yeah. It's vaguely related.
So, then... You are certainly Memphis, and she is certainly Helena?
What about the others? Are they all... Or are they stuck in the resculpting phase?
Consciousness determines existence, and cognition determines the self. Does anything else matter?
...I suppose not. Helena has gone a long way without realizing it.
Yeah... She did it for us. For all those who we've lost.
That's why we've got to save her.
And rest assured, I'm confident that we can save her!
Whew... Focus, Boise. You have to rescue Helena...
Take it easy, Boise. Victory is gonna be ours!
Hm? Cleveland? Why aren't you with the rest of the Council?
Hiryuu originally dragged me out here. Said she saw you all looking gloomy and wanted me to go encourage you.
Anyway, I noticed that you're just too worried about stuff. It's doing the opposite of helping you.
You can't go thinking about what'll happen if you lose when you haven't even had a real fight yet.
Yeah... You're right. Let's give this all we've got, Cleveland.
Hell yeah! Knights of the Sea, sail forth!
*sigh*... There are quite a lot of them. All bunched up.
Enforcers, advance!
KABOOOM!
Ah, this model... Activate VII=VI linkage.
Commencing annihilation!
KABOOOM!
It's you this time...
Activate VII=XIV linkage.
KABOOOM!
Hah... There's no need to activate a linkage this time.
I'll just push my way through.
This is good. The load on the Veil is rapidly diminishing.
Temperance, Hermit, assist Star with resetting the Star Barrier.
- Okay.  - Got it.
scripts.actorName: Arbiter: Temperance XIV & Arbiter: The Hermit IX

scripts.say: Magician, start preparing on your end as well.
Understood. Rediverting performance now.
And next...
Moon, use the War Protocol Moon vessel to contact {playername}. Say the time is ripe to go to the Anchorage National Observatory.
Also, that you'd better get ready if you're going to meet Helena again.
Rumey's Resistance fleet rushed back for headquarters at flank speed.
Rumey, Commander. Continuing along this direct route will bring us into treacherous waters.
(Treacherous waters?)
How much of a threat does this route pose to our main fleet?
There is a level of risk. An acceptable level, though, given the size of our force.
So you're saying...
Every second counts. We stay the course.
Roger that!
KABOOOM!
ROOOOOAR!
Oh no... We're going as fast as we can, but they're faster!
This horde is even stronger than the last!
Rumey, they're testing us and whittling away our forces all at once.
They attack our headquarters AND intercept us when we return to defend it... Something must be leading them, that's for sure.
It's too dangerous to press on. Rumey, requesting a change of course.
You think there's a Chief out there? Those things don't show up often ever since we lost the Sirens.
The last one was decades ago. I know that you're concerned, but you must be overthinking it.
We're halfway through already, and we've sustained close to no damage.
Your prudence is commendable, yes, but our defenses at HQ are thin without our main fleet.
We have no choice but to risk it. Keep moving forward, now!
KABOOOM!
Commander! Rumey! The attacks from our flanks are too strong! Our formation is breaking!
I will cover the rear! Have all ships reform 30 nautical miles ahead!
Understood! I'll relay that at once!
Commander, lead with the command ship and oversee the reformation effort! As soon as it's complete, proceed to base immediately!
If they know our plans, then their next move...
Rumey. Are extradimensionals known to attack via self-destruction?
They're beasts. They follow only their instincts – never would they end their own lives for a greater goal.
They flee in the face of overwhelming odds, and it's extremely rare for them to fight to the death. If they ever did self-destruct, it would be...
...Because their leader forced them to.
Good lord! But that can't–
KABOOOM!
Amidst the explosion of the mass-produced ship, my consciousness is thrown into the empty abyss.
SHUFFLE...
Then, I hear the sound of cards shuffling.
Our counteroffensive went smoothly. The enemy markers on the monitor vanished one after the next, and victory seemed but a shot away.
But right at that moment, a shocking development occurred.
A star overhead suddenly glows blindingly brightly, its magnified radiance lighting up half of the night sky in the blink of an eye.
The white heavens become diffused with innumerable blue lights that flicker in and out of existence. It's like someone has inverted the colors of the night.
A strange sound – like encroaching waves – rings out, resonating with everything and everyone and shaking the very soul.
Oh my god... Is that a Lord class?! I thought they were a myth!
A Lord class?
A being that surpasses even the Chief class... The true leader of the extradimensionals.
The Star Beast is its name... It has only appeared three times throughout history.
Every appearance has been marked with disaster.
That makes this the fourth time...
How did you deal with it the previous three?
The first time, we threw all of humanity's golden age creations at it. The second, the Sirens displayed their final glory.
The third – we could do nothing but witness its fury.
This is looking grim.
Countless feelers appear, reaching into the sky as though trying to stitch it and the sea together.
The waves grow strong and furious, striking fear into the heart of every shipgirl.
Star Beast...
Back then... It was you!
Ahahahaha... Finally, I've found you!
Yes... It's time!
Time to take revenge for what you did to my sisters!
I was weak back then – but not anymore!
Your death will be the Admiral Hipper class' crowning achievement!
Hipper gazed up at the vast sky and declared her intent for all to hear.
No, Hipper! Calm down!
It's no use. She won't listen to us.
That doesn't mean we're going to let her kill herself.
All units, support Hipper with all you have!
KABOOOM!
The cannon fire vanished like fireflies in the black, starry sky.

SHUFFLE...
Then, I hear the sound of cards shuffling.
Z52 dashes bravely through the herd of extradimensionals.
I switch from the warship and board a high-speed boat, following her wake.
Thunderheart, burst!
KABOOOM!
Sensing a change in the battle, the extradimensionals extend their feelers to try to cut off our path.
Too slow!
Thunderheart, burn and send 'em flying!
KABOOOM!
She breaches through the wall of tentacles before its completion.
BZZZZT!
A strange sound suddenly rings out, and for an instant, it feels like the boat's engine and my heart completely stop.
The next moment, though, that sensation vanishes like it was nothing.
I felt that. The enemy's feeling pressured.
That means our plan is working.
Relax. I'm not going anywhere.
Almost at the target! Pterosaurs, go!
The drones scatter the incoming enemies and carry off my boat into the Eternal Star.
Z52, regrouping with original fleet!
Here's hoping this will work!
Good luck, Commander!
Sometime later...
I turn my attention to the third control panel in the hall.
Huh. The Wall of Midgard – a protective barrier that combines offense and defense.
(I knew it. This Mirror Sea isn't just here to camouflage the headquarters.)
(Was the offensive part of it never completed? Seems we'll have to rely on its defensive features.)
Following the operation manual left in the data logs, I issue a set of instructions to the structure via the panel.
My credentials are verified without issue, and the orders are executed one by one.
The Mirror Sea's invisible boundary line starts to warp, creating what appears to be a sort of barrier.
Up next – station four.
I examine the fourth control panel while the defenses activate.
Okay, logs, logs... This is the energy tower.
Zero damage sustained. I'm amazed, considering how long it's stood there.
Huh... It's called the Tower of Midgard.
(Feels like I've seen that name somewhere before. Could it be linked to my lost memories?)
I start looking for what secret knowledge the Tower contains.
Damn. The logs and operating access are locked.
Let's see... It can only be accessed once Jörmungandr reaches 40%?
"Jörmungandr"? What is that?
What were the Sirens trying to do here?
Despite looking around all over, I fail to find anything that could clue me in.
BZZZZT!
Right then, the shockwaves of the Star Beast appearing transmit through the hall.
A star overhead suddenly glows blindingly brightly, its magnified radiance lighting up half of the night sky in the blink of an eye.
That's quicker than last time! Did it catch on to what I'm doing?
Fine! I'll have to play the hand I've built up, then!
Eternal Star, commence attack!
Blue stars glimmer in the inverted sky.
A Lord class... It did appear after all.
The Mirror Sea is changing. The Commander must have succeeded.
A-are we going to be okay?
We shall see. Fighting is our only choice.
Countless feelers appear, reaching into the sky as though trying to stitch it and the sea together.
The Eternal Star's barrage of shells blow them to smithereens. The pieces fall back down into the sea like hailstones.
BZZZZT!
There is that odd sound again. Beams of energy are fired at me – but the Mirror Sea's protective barrier blocks them all.
It worked.
Hah! Not so tough anymore! Your reign of terror is OVER!
I can finally, finally have my revenge!
Calm down, Hipper. Stick to the plan.
Yeah, I know.
Although... that barrier probably won't hold up.
It's sufficient to stall for time. Now we must come up with a countermeasure.
All ships, focus fire on the tentacles! Stop the Star Beast's descent!
KABOOOM!
What was that noise? Did the energy tower just explode?!
Curses... It overheated! The barrier held, but the tower didn't!
You people have done more than enough.
Now it's my turn. I'm taking that thing head-on.
Time to take revenge for what you did to my sisters!
I was weak back then – but not anymore!
Your death will be the Admiral Hipper class' crowning achievement!
Hipper gazed up at the vast sky and declared her intent for all to hear.

The waters of the Mirror Sea begin to shift.
Its normally invisible boundary distorts, manifesting something like a barrier.
I had no idea the Mirror Sea had such a hidden function... Another miracle wrought by the Commander.
Things are going surprisingly well so far!
The Commander's predictions of enemy numbers and positioning were spot-on.
It's almost like you can see the future! Frankly, it's kinda creepy...
I'm just glad the Commander's on our side.
Everything is going exactly the way you said... Then that must mean...
The Star Beast will appear. Steel yourselves.
Our counteroffensive went smoothly. The enemy markers on the monitor vanished one after the next, and victory seemed but a shot away.
But right at that moment, a shocking development occurred.
A star overhead suddenly glows blindingly brightly, its magnified radiance lighting up half of the night sky in the blink of an eye.
The white heavens become diffused with innumerable blue lights that flicker in and out of existence. It's like someone has inverted the colors of the night.
A Lord class... It did appear after all.
A-are we going to be okay?
We shall see. Fighting is our only choice.
Strange noises come in waves, seemingly shaking all the world through to our very souls.
But the force is blocked by the Wall of Midgard, doing little more than causing some ripples on the barrier.
Countless feelers appear, reaching into the sky as though trying to stitch it and the sea together.
The Eternal Star's barrage of shells blow them to smithereens. The pieces fall back down into the sea like hailstones.
(So far, so good. But this is where the battle truly begins.)
Hipper, are you ready?
I've been waiting for this for a long time! Let me at it!
Everyone, focus your attacks on the Lord class!
KABOOOOM!
Follow my lead! We will synchronize our strikes!
Cover Hipper and secure a route to victory!
KABOOOOM!
The cannon fire vanished like fireflies in the black, starry sky.

I'll defeat you... not just to avenge my sisters, but for the sake of a bright future for the Admiral Hipper class!
PUZVSLUA PUZLJAZ
BZZZZT!
When she leaves the safety of the barrier, the Star Beast launches an attack.
However, the crushing noise is erased by soft light.
Bullying poor Hipper? Not on my watch.
Heheh☆ Hipper! Let's punish this big lug together!
Two people thought long lost appear on the scene.
The girls on Hipper's flanks point their guns in the same direction.
Eugen, Blücher... Shouldn't the two of you be...
No way. This isn't real...
Are you ghosts? Hallucinations? Or...?
Geez~ Settle down, Sis!
You're not wrong, but that doesn't mean you're right!
Well, uh, maybe you are actually wrong...
Aargh, I don't understand it well enough to explain!
Eugen, help me out here!
Basically, your wishes took form as us.
You wished to make a new future for the Admiral Hipper class. How could we let you do it alone?
Is it... really you?
Yeah, we're back. Only for a while, though.
Hipper... Thanks for all you've done in our stead.
